Some people say that first impressions are almost impossible to change, but I do not agree. People’s lives often go through many changes, and those changes can lead to new goals and better futures. Although changing can be difficult for different reasons, it is not unattainable. Everyone has their own aims, and with effort it is possible to change habits, attitudes, or the opinions others have of us. New beginnings are like windows of opportunity: if we take them, they can open many doors. For me, starting a new way of life with a clear purpose helps me improve and reach the dreams I imagine. Impressions are not fixed; they can be altered because life gives us chances to grow, to refine our goals, and to plan steps that improve our abilities.

First, changes often bring fresh opportunities. A new job, a course, or even a project can act like a door to different experiences and skills. By taking these chances we learn more and can apply what we learn in practical situations. As technology and society progress, more paths become available for learning and personal development. These opportunities make it easier to change how others see us and how we see ourselves, because we gain new knowledge and demonstrate new capabilities.

Second, improving our goals and dreams is a strong reason why impressions can change. When we refine our plans and work to put them into practice, we become more confident and able. It is important to focus on learning from mistakes instead of giving up because of them. People sometimes stop trying after failing, but the best path to improvement is to study what went wrong and make adjustments. Over time, consistent effort and small improvements can change how others judge our abilities and character.

Third, making clear plans helps us develop the skills needed to realize our ideas. Writing down objectives and the steps to reach them makes progress measurable and real. Thinking through different options and choosing what fits us best leads to better development in any area of life. Good planning can also improve our financial situation if it helps us find or keep better work. In this way, changing our habits and following a plan can gradually change the impression people have of us, especially in professional and family life.

In conclusion, I believe impressions can be changed. Although it can be hard at first, taking opportunities, learning from mistakes, and making realistic plans allow us to grow and alter how others perceive us. Change begins with a decision to act, and with persistence anyone can improve their life and reach their goals. If people are willing to change for the better, they will find that old impressions can become new realities.

Our manager usually had a harsh manner and was often short-tempered with the staff, but I tried not to let his behavior affect me; I kept smiling and stayed friendly. One day he came to work in a very different state — devastated because his wife had been hospitalized with cancer. I asked if we could talk, and he agreed. I simply wanted him to know we were there for him. Sadly, his wife passed away. During that difficult period, our team showed him constant support and kept a hopeful, comforting attitude, telling him his wife would no longer suffer and would rest in peace. He was deeply grateful for our kindness and, to show his appreciation, offered most of us raises. Since then he has become a much kinder person. Many of us still work there and earn more than before. That experience showed me how a positive approach can influence others and even change a workplace.

A positive attitude also helps in family crises. My family once faced a severe money problem after my father lost his job. We had not paid rent for about four months and risked losing our home. My father was very upset and spent weeks looking for work without success. My mother comforted him, saying, “Don’t worry, we will get through this as we always do. I’m here with you.” Her support and calm words changed his mood; he smiled, thanked her, took the car keys, and started looking for work again with renewed energy. He soon found a job that paid a little more than the previous one, and our financial problems were solved. My father’s response showed how encouragement from a loved one can help someone recover hope and take action.

Believing in yourself can be difficult, but encouragement from others can make a big difference. In tenth grade I had an algebra teacher who constantly told us to trust our abilities. At the start of the year many students were discouraged and failed the first quarter because we were afraid to try problems we didn’t fully understand. Our teacher talked to us, pushed us to attempt tasks even when they seemed hard, and reminded us that we could improve. Gradually our attitudes changed: we paid attention, practiced more, and began to believe in ourselves. By the second quarter many students raised their scores from around 50 up to 90. I am still grateful to that teacher—she cared about us, supported us, and believed in our potential. Her positive influence made a real difference in our learning and confidence.

Some people think positivity is only for important or happy moments, but I disagree. Keeping a positive attitude consistently helps us face difficulties and find solutions. Adults at home—grandparents, parents, siblings—should set a good example so children learn to be confident and optimistic. For these reasons, I believe a positive attitude is essential in life.

Online learning programs offered by schools can bring both benefits and drawbacks. Schools handle these programs in different ways; some do not offer them at all, while others rely on them heavily. People have varying opinions about taking classes online. Some believe it is a good idea because of the flexibility, while others think it creates problems. For example, online courses let you move at your own pace and not wait for classmates. On the other hand, technical problems like slow or failing Wi-Fi can make it hard to complete assignments, and students may miss the social environment of a regular classroom or fail to turn in their work.

Students often find it harder to finish assigned work when learning online. If you run into a problem, you might not have a teacher available right away to explain it. Some websites or resources give incorrect solutions, and relying on these can lead to wrong answers on assignments. You might find videos that explain the topic, but many subjects don’t have enough helpful video tutorials. In a physical classroom, a teacher can show you the steps and clear up confusion immediately, which usually helps you understand better. With online classes, teachers may not be online when you need them, and students sometimes put work off and never complete it. This makes meeting deadlines more difficult for many learners.

Being around classmates of the same age also helps learning. In person, students can compare study methods, ask each other for help, and form study groups. Online schooling is mostly between you and a screen; even if you have friends, they may not be taking the same class, so you cannot easily work or study together. Online students may miss chances to meet new people or to socialize during class time. Often, the people you interact with online are older or not part of your peer group. A classroom environment provides shared experiences and support that can make learning easier, while studying alone at home may feel isolating.

Online courses sometimes assign a lot of work to be completed in a short time. When you don’t understand the material, this can be very challenging. Doing assignments properly is important to learn what the course teaches; copying something that only looks similar online will not help. Some students become lazy and leave tasks until the last minute, which harms their grades. If a student consistently delays work, they might fail or have to repeat the course. Home distractions and personal problems can pull attention away from schoolwork, which makes completing assignments before the due date even harder.

Schools give students options to attend classes in different ways, which can increase access and free up time. However, some students may take advantage of this freedom and avoid doing the work. Life can be unpredictable, and without a teacher present, learning certain subjects can be difficult. In the end, students must decide what works best for them. Online classes can be helpful for some, but they are often challenging — lacking peer interaction and immediate help — and do not always lead to success.

I agree with Ralph Waldo Emerson’s idea. Many people act as if completing college or getting a degree automatically makes them adults, but if you return home and keep living with your parents, they will often continue to see you as their child. Until you start building your own life — finding steady work, saving money, and becoming independent — your parents may treat you the same way they did when you were very young. I believe this is what Emerson meant.

To the wider world, you become an adult when you have responsibilities of your own: a car, a house, a job, or a family to care for. When you are responsible for others, you begin to put their needs first the way your parents did for you. Then the story repeats from the other side: you are the one telling the story and protecting younger people. Even as a parent, you will always see your children as your children no matter how old they get. I noticed this when I watched my older sister take care of her daughter. That experience made me start to view life differently.

I left home at fifteen. It was difficult at first, but moving out made me grow up faster than staying comfortable at home would have. For me, becoming an adult meant choosing my own path and stopping worrying about how others see me. Family remained my top priority — first, second, and third.

I think the healthiest way to grow is to focus on yourself and your responsibilities. You do not necessarily have to move out to prove you are mature; sometimes changing how you see the world and taking responsibility is enough. Maturity is not just a number; it is about making decisions for yourself and caring for those close to you. I say this from personal experience of growing up early.

I believe schools should offer an after-school homework club because many students struggle to finish or understand their assignments. When homework is confusing, it’s hard to know what to do, and having a place to work after school would help lots of students actually complete their tasks. Some people think homework is not very important, but it often counts for a portion of the final grade — even 10 percent can make a real difference. Finishing that one assignment you didn’t get before could be the thing that helps you pass a quiz or do better on a test.

Middle school students have a lot to manage. With seven classes, it is difficult to keep up, and some teachers assign more than one task in a night. That adds up quickly and makes it hard to finish everything on time. An after-school club would give students a reliable time to concentrate on homework for multiple classes and reduce the pressure of juggling so many deadlines.

Another benefit is that students could ask questions and get help on things they did not understand in class. A teacher or a trained helper can explain the lesson again so students actually learn the material, instead of just copying answers. This kind of support could raise grades — moving someone from a B to an A — because they would understand the work and be better prepared for tests.

The club would also help the school. If more students turn in completed homework, the school’s performance may improve. Teachers would be more confident that students are doing their own work and not just finding answers elsewhere. For some students who can do the work but struggle to meet deadlines, having time after school to finish assignments would solve that problem. It would create a cleaner system for submitting work and reduce excuses.

Finally, this club could lower stress for many students. Knowing there is a set time and place to finish assignments would free up the rest of the afternoon and evening. Students could relax or take part in other activities once their homework is done. For those who often miss parts of class or don’t understand the lesson, the after-school help would make schoolwork less overwhelming and more manageable.

In conclusion, an after-school homework club would be a valuable addition to middle schools. Homework plays an important role in learning and grades, even when students think it does not matter. With extra time and support available, students would understand lessons better, improve their grades, meet deadlines more easily, and feel less stressed. That is why I think schools should create a homework club.

Ralph Waldo Emerson once said that being yourself in a world that constantly tries to change you is the greatest achievement. I agree with this idea and will explain why staying true to who you are leads to real success.

First, let us clarify the meaning of "accomplish." To accomplish something is to achieve or complete a goal honestly and fully. Living genuinely, rather than pretending to be someone else, helps you reach your true aims. I will illustrate this with an example.

I know of a woman who tried to fake a wealthy, glamorous life to get a high-paying director job. She dressed and acted like a rich person and even borrowed large sums of money to support the image: expensive cars and houses she could not actually afford. Everyone believed she was wealthy, and she assumed this would guarantee her the position. She competed against another candidate who did not pretend to be rich. This second woman was poor but had the right experience and real talent.

After weeks of consideration, the decision day came. The selection panel reviewed both candidates and revealed some evidence. They exposed that one of the applicants had borrowed nearly $500,000 and used loans to create a false image of success. The panel explained that giving the company’s leadership to someone who had been living a lie would be risky — she might harm the organization through dishonesty or fraud. Because of this, they offered the job to the woman who had been honest about her background and had demonstrated real ability.

This story shows that pretending to be someone else rarely brings lasting success. The woman who remained true to herself attained the position through merit, while the one who faked her life ended up exposed and humiliated. Being authentic may be harder at times, but it leads to genuine accomplishment. In a world that pressures us to change, staying yourself is indeed the greatest achievement.

One question has been asked during a long time. Is it better to work alone or to work in a group?

Most of the people and analysts have got the conclusion that working in groups could be more beneficial.

For example, if you are planning either something as big as a school event, or something as simple as a classroom presentation, there is occasions when you run out of ideas. You can count in the group. They are going to be there giving diverse solutions to the problem, otherwise, by yourself you could be struggling like if you are in road with no exit.

Working in a group sometimes can make you relax, laugh and bring positivism, even in challenging moments or when you are facing stress. Every time you have to work in this way, you do not spend boring moments. There will be always something to talk about. You and your team would be saving memories that in a future would be a moment of laugh.

Another fact about working in group is that you get to finish the work in a faster. More people working in the a series of things in a quickly way than just one, makes a big difference. It will give space to the creativity, where you can practice more, give details to the work or even do new creations.

Because you are working in a team you do not focus only in "I" you open your mind and start thinking in "we". This is going to be useful in the future, when you go out to the real world. Working with other people, you have to deal with different personalities and thoughts. The team working abilities are going to be place in your mind.

When as a team all your tasks are completed you will find a great euphoria in the results. It is going to make everyone proud of themselves and also it is going to be a method to keep pushing them up and never give up.

Sometimes when you get to work in a group it might sound or seem a difficult task. But instead, you learned new experiences and new abilities. It become a helpful tool to develop character and to grow as a person. You have to learn how to speak with the people and how to tell your ideas in a clear manner. That is why many people agreed that working in teams brings more benefits than just working alone.

For a long time people have asked whether it is better to work alone or as part of a team. Many observers and ordinary people believe that collaborating with others brings greater advantages.

One reason for this view is that teams offer a variety of perspectives. Different members contribute distinct ideas and ways of thinking, which can be very helpful when you face difficulties. For example, while preparing a large school event or a simple class presentation, it is common to run out of ideas. In a group you can rely on others to suggest alternatives, whereas working alone may feel like being on a road with no exit.

Working with others can also make the process more enjoyable and less stressful. Teamwork often brings laughter, encouragement and a positive atmosphere, even in demanding moments. When you are part of a group you rarely experience long boring periods, and you build shared memories that you can smile about later.

Another advantage is that tasks are usually finished faster. When several people share different parts of a project, the work moves more quickly than when one person does everything. This also creates room for creativity: team members can refine details, practice parts of the task, or produce new ideas together.

Teamwork teaches you to think beyond yourself. Instead of focusing only on “I,” you begin to consider “we.” This mindset is useful later in life, since real workplaces require cooperation with people who have different personalities and viewpoints. Learning to work in a team develops important collaborative skills.

When a team completes its tasks successfully, the result often brings strong satisfaction. This shared pride motivates everyone to keep trying and to improve. Although working in a group can sometimes seem challenging, it teaches new skills and helps you grow. You learn how to communicate clearly and present your ideas effectively. For these reasons many people conclude that group work offers more benefits than working alone.

I agree that first impressions are very difficult to change. A first impression is tied to the very first moment you notice something or someone, and that initial reaction is often strong and memorable. Even if a similar situation happens later, it rarely feels the same as the original moment. Because that first feeling is linked to your immediate experience, it becomes a fixed reference point that you remember and sometimes want to preserve.

For example, imagine walking down the street and seeing someone dressed in a striking or unusual way. Their appearance immediately draws attention because it stands out from what people usually see. Others may begin to talk about this person, offering opinions or making quick judgments based on clothing alone. Some people may be curious and want to learn more about the person’s background or culture, while others may simply judge without trying to understand. In any case, the first impression formed in that situation is powerful and spreads quickly among observers.

We encounter first impressions constantly because we are always surrounded by different people—family, friends, classmates, colleagues, and strangers. Each new meeting can create a first impression, and because these meetings happen so often and in so many places, we keep forming these instant assessments. It does not matter where you are; new faces, new actions, or new styles can trigger an immediate reaction. Over time, you collect many of these initial impressions, and some of them remain in your mind.

Often, first impressions influence what we do next. You might tell friends about someone you noticed or use a striking example to explain a point. Sometimes a first impression motivates personal change: seeing something impressive in another person can inspire you to try something different for yourself. In that way, a first impression can have positive effects by encouraging growth or new experiences. Even if the original impression is brief, it can linger and shape later choices.

In conclusion, first impressions are usually hard to alter because they are unique and tied to a specific moment. You can change your opinion over time or reconsider your initial feelings, but the first impression itself remains a distinct memory. If you encounter the same person or situation again, it will feel different because you already know what to expect. Despite their limitations, first impressions can still help us understand people and learn about different ways of life. They offer quick insights that, when followed by openness and reflection, can enrich our view of others.

Last week I had a math test during first period. I had studied well, but that morning I overslept and realized I was running late for school. I missed the bus and had to walk the entire way, which left me exhausted and anxious. Because of that, I did poorly on the exam. If classes had been online, I could have taken the test from home and avoided all that stress. Online lessons can prevent these kinds of problems and also save time. Some people argue that learning from home is not helpful because students might not understand the lessons or assignments without face-to-face help, and so they could fall behind. Still, I believe students benefit from online classes since they can join from wherever they are—if they are ill or away from home—and they can make better use of their time for work, extra courses, or other activities.

Those who oppose remote learning have valid concerns. They point out that students sometimes struggle to follow lectures or complete tasks during online sessions. For example, a student might be given a project but not know how to approach it, or they may miss the meaning of a topic explained in a virtual lecture. Without immediate, in-person support, some learners could find it hard to keep up and perform well.

Despite these worries, being able to attend classes from home offers real advantages. When students are sick, they don’t have to miss lessons; they can join the class online and keep up with the material. Likewise, if someone is staying at a relative’s house or travelling, they can still attend school remotely. In my case, if I had been able to take that math test from home, my oversleeping would not have ruined my performance.

Another benefit of online classes is the time saved. High school students who study from home can plan their days more flexibly, giving them more hours to work part-time jobs or to take additional courses that support their future goals. For example, not having to commute would allow me to work more on weekdays and save money for college. I could also finish school assignments faster and enroll in extra classes or pursue hobbies that interest me.

In conclusion, allowing students to attend classes online brings several benefits. It provides an option to study while sick or when away from home, and it helps students organize their time better so they can work more, take extra courses, or enjoy other activities. Overall, online education can make school life more manageable and give students more opportunities.

My grandmother often told me that failing is not the end; what matters is getting back up and trying again. A decision means choosing an option or forming a judgment about a question or problem. People benefit when they make their own choices. I believe individuals should decide for themselves because it is their right, because they learn from the results of their actions, and because they can think and form opinions independently.

Some people say it is better to seek guidance when making decisions because advisers may have more experience. I disagree. Many people fought and even died to gain personal freedoms, and today we have the privilege to speak and act for ourselves. For that reason, no one should let others take over choices that belong to them. People do not necessarily need outside guidance to reach a good decision.

First, making choices is a basic right. For example, a citizen of the United States may decide to file for divorce after discovering infidelity. He went to court to make it official because this is his legal right and a deeply personal matter. He does not need someone else to decide for him or to approve his feelings. In short, the ability to make personal decisions is a freedom everyone should be able to exercise.

Second, people can make mistakes, but they are also capable of correcting them. For instance, a young person gave in to peer pressure and tried drugs. Later she realized this was wrong and harmful to her health, and she stopped using them. Society and friends can push someone in the wrong direction, but each person can still say no and change their behavior. Learning from errors helps people grow and avoid repeating the same mistakes.

Finally, everyone has different beliefs and viewpoints, so individuals should be allowed to choose for themselves. For example, parents can teach their child to tell right from wrong, but the child will still use their own judgment when making decisions. People are unique and may disagree with others, but disagreement does not automatically make one side right and the other wrong. Respect for other people’s choices is important.

In conclusion, making decisions is a privilege won by past generations, mistakes are part of learning, and everyone has the capacity to think for themselves. These reasons show that citizens do not always need external guidance to decide. We should respect other people’s choices and not judge them, and remember that you can act on your decisions even when others doubt you.

Do you think failure is useful? In this essay I will discuss failure and success in life. When people fail, they often feel unhappy, try to stay motivated, or become angry with themselves.

First, many people feel upset when they fail because they did their best and expected to succeed. They did not imagine failing, so the result can be shocking and sometimes even lead to tears.

Second, some people try to keep their motivation after a first failure. They stay positive and tell themselves they will do better next time. This attitude means they do not lose hope after one setback.

Third, a person can become angry with themselves because they believe they did not perform well. They may be frustrated even by small mistakes. However, that frustration can help them learn from their errors and improve.

In conclusion, although failure can seem bad for some people, it can become a step toward success for those who stay motivated and learn from their mistakes.

Ensuring that students have their career in mind by the time they enter high school will allow them to learn more and prepare for college. It will also help them be an inspiration for many other teenagers and encourage others to think about the importance of having a good education and career.

When students reach eighth grade in middle school, they often begin exploring different careers and forming ideas about what they might want to do in the future. Young people should be allowed to choose the path that fits their interests. Too often parents insist on a particular profession, leaving teenagers with little real choice. Today’s adolescents deserve the freedom to decide what to study. High school is a time to develop many skills and learn a variety of subjects that will help them later on. Gaining different abilities prepares students for a range of jobs and helps them cope with unexpected challenges. Encouraging children to follow their interests from an early age makes learning more natural; their thinking and motivation improve day by day. For example, interested students often look for information and ask advice from people already working in the field they are considering. After middle and high school, young people should feel ready to begin college and make decisions that suit their own goals.

In many parts of the world, however, teenagers do not have the same chances to study. In countries with weak educational systems or few resources—such as some nations in Central America and parts of Africa—many young people leave school to work and support their families. Their schooling can be poor or interrupted, which is one reason families try to reach the United States, hoping for a better future. Children who arrive in the U.S. often carry big dreams and strong motivation; they want to make their families proud by earning a meaningful degree and building a stable life. In places where the population is growing fast and jobs are scarce, even a diploma may not guarantee work, and some parents discourage education with comments like “school won’t lead to anything.” When families block young people’s hopes, it can cause serious social problems. Parents should support their children’s education and help them explore career choices while they are still young.

Thinking about the future early on has a clear positive effect. In many parts of the world teenagers do not plan ahead or care about school and work, but in the U.S. there are more opportunities to get a good education, a healthy life, and secure employment. Young people who know their career interests by the time they enter high school can focus their learning, prepare for college, and set themselves up for success. These students are likely to find good jobs, become role models for others, and inspire their communities. Schools and families should help students consider their careers early so they can learn more, make better choices, and encourage other young people to value education.

My main talents are drawing, painting, coloring, and writing. These are the things I enjoy most. I like making cartoons, sketching pictures, adding color, and writing stories. Last year I took a lot of art classes and joined several art clubs. For a while I wanted to be a professional cartoonist, but this year I decided to focus more on writing. Even so, I’m still good at art and I plan to take art again in ninth grade. I often use my art and writing when I am bored, whether I am at home or at school.

When it comes to writing, I want to create novels and books that many people can read. I have been taking writing classes in the summer to improve. I also started as a cartoonist last year, creating cartoons and short pieces for the school newspaper. At school I joined the animation club and drew scenes for our projects. I enjoyed that, so I also joined the yearbook club and wrote captions under photos to explain what was happening. In third block I had FACS (family and consumer sciences), where I used art to decorate cakes, cupcakes, and even ice cream. All of these activities showed me that art fits into many parts of my life.

One of my favorite things to write about is the story of Transformers: Dark of the Moon. I like graphic novels and that movie is one of my favorites. The beginning of the story is about the war on Cybertron, and the rest talks about adventures in space. What I enjoy most about writing is expressing words and feelings. I also like writing poems because they help me think about emotions in a different way.

Here are some specific reasons I like writing:
- Writing can make a strong impression on readers.
- Writing can include both facts and personal opinions.
- Writing also allows room for poems.

Art is everywhere around us. It appears in many places and connects with writing in several ways. Good writing uses the right vocabulary and correct spelling, so it’s important to check your spelling after you finish an article or an essay. Graphic novels, for example, combine art and text: the author draws speech bubbles for characters to show when they are happy, sad, or feeling another emotion. Text formatting, like bold type, can show what is most important. When someone reads a book, the words and images work together to share the story.

In conclusion, I will keep thinking about my talents and what they mean to me. I still care about both art and writing, and I want to continue using them. For example, I draw and write comics. That is what matters most to me. The end.

Dear Manager,

I am writing to ask if I could visit your company to find out whether a career there would be a good fit for me.

I would like to see the kinds of jobs that are available and learn more about what each role involves. Seeing the work in person will help me understand how tasks are carried out and what skills are needed.

Large companies can hire many employees, which helps work move faster. A visit would let students experience what it feels like to work in a company, and to understand what it takes to be a manager. For example, it would be useful to know typical working hours, how long shifts last, when lunch breaks are scheduled, and how daily routines are organized. You could also show how the workplace is arranged so people can find what they need quickly to finish products for sale.

I have many practical questions that a visit could answer. How large can a company be — are there legal or physical limits on the space it can use? What does it cost to build a factory or office? Do companies need remodeling or recertification every few years, such as every five or six years? Is it better to build in an urban area or in the countryside? When do suppliers bring materials, and how often? How much do materials and other running costs typically amount to, so a company does not spend too much and risk going bankrupt?

If a company runs out of money or materials, what options does it have? Does it need to be sold? How high are utility bills like electricity, and how do companies manage these expenses? What happens if products are faulty — can the company get into legal trouble or lose customers? I understand that companies differ in size because some sell faster, earn more, and can afford better equipment and more staff.

I am also curious about intellectual property: if one company copies another’s idea, are there fines, or could people go to jail? Do factories operate every day, including holidays like Christmas and New Year? How much vacation do employees get? Are machines switched off on festive days?

What are the rules for sick leave? Do employees need to call a manager before staying home, or is it accepted if they do not show up? If someone falls ill while working, is there a replacement for the shift until they recover? In the event of a fire, does the company get compensation for damaged equipment and lost stock?

A visit would be very helpful for students who want to experience being an employee, a manager, or a specialist in finance. Learning how companies are run and how to manage money could prevent future financial problems.

Thank you for considering my request.

Sincerely,

Should students finish high school in three years so they can start college and enter the workforce earlier? Many students, parents and teachers support shortening high school, and I agree. Finishing high school in three years helps young people graduate from university sooner, find jobs earlier, and become independent at a younger age.

In my country, El Salvador, high school already lasts three years. For example, my older sister left high school at seventeen, went on to university and will complete her nursing degree at twenty-one. Because she started sooner, she will enter the job market earlier than if high school had taken longer. I am currently in high school and expect to finish at nineteen under the current system. That feels late to me, especially if I choose a career that requires eight years of study; a shorter high school period would speed up the whole process.

At my school we held a vote to see what people thought about keeping high school at three years. Seventy percent agreed that three years is better. Teachers argued that a shorter program gives students more chances to graduate quickly, which matters because many students repeat grades. My brother is an example: he failed a year and now must repeat ninth grade, so instead of four years he will spend five years in high school. This shows how delays can add up and keep young people from starting their careers.

My mother also finished high school at seventeen. She became a doctor at twenty-five and later trained as a heart specialist, finishing that course by thirty. Because she completed high school early, she had time to study at night while working, and now she has two good jobs and a better life. Her path suggests that earlier secondary graduation can open more opportunities and lead to greater stability sooner.

For these reasons, I believe a three-year high school is preferable. Some districts disagree, but I think they underestimate how much earlier graduation can help students gain qualifications and find work. I hope more places will adopt three-year high schools so young people can start their adult lives sooner.

The sound of children laughing while playing video games is familiar to many. Gaming is so common that even people in their thirties still enjoy it. But are video games truly that enjoyable for adults as well as kids?

Why people enjoy gaming

To begin with, children find video games thrilling. The fast pace, the sense of danger, and constant surprises make each session exciting. For many youngsters, video games offer an escape and a way to blow off steam. While some titles can be stressful or maddening, others are calming and comforting — think of simple puzzle games or friendly adventures like Tetris or Pokémon.

There is a huge variety of games available, from Fortnite and League of Legends to Roblox and countless others. Kids flock to these games because they are entertaining. In a way, they gather around games the way a pack of wolves searches together for food. Playing also engages several senses: sight to follow the action, hearing to pick up sounds and cues, and touch to control the game. This combination gives players a kind of mental workout, even if they may not realize it. Adults, too, use these same senses when they play.

The drawbacks

Video games are not without problems. Staring at screens for long periods can strain the eyes. Excessive gaming may hurt attention spans and can make some people withdraw from the outside world or avoid social interactions. There are definite risks that come with too much play.

In the end, children often play without worrying about consequences, while adults usually understand the potential downsides but choose to play anyway. There are many reasons games are both enjoyable and harmful, yet for people of all ages they remain a popular way to have fun. Why do you think kids and adults play video games?

She turns it in and thinks she did well, but it turns out that it is the opposite. She has the chance to retake it and is taking the chance. Sometimes expectations don't go the way people would like, but that doesn't mean eventually the expectation won't get met. It just means to keep trying.

Another reason on why failure can bring success is because it gives thought of improvement. Everyone knows the saying "You learn from your mistakes." That saying is very true. If something goes wrong because of the way it was dealt with, will the same mistake happen again? Of course not! People see when they mess up or fail after it happens and will try to do better. That is improvement and it's leading you to success. Then we will know where to start and where to fix things. It's a part of succeeding. People who have succeeded can tell others that without at least one fail, they would not have made it to where they are now.

Last but not least, it gives you experience. If we didn't fail there would be no experience for the next goal. Having that experience of failure will help. When the goal is met and finally succeeded then there will be an amazing story to tell, especially because failure was around. Speak on the obstacles that were faced and how to get through without giving up. Having this experience and speaking about it can influence others as well. Maybe some people also have failed but they want to give up; encourage others that failing doesn't mean you still can't succeed.

To conclude, failure can be a big step to success if used the right way. Don't sit there and give up because failing is a way closer to the goal. Use failure as motivation, thought of improvement, and an opportunity to have an experience. In this case, failure is a great thing.

Can failure lead to success?

Winston Churchill once noted that achieving success often means moving through a series of failures without losing your enthusiasm. Many people who aim high would agree with this idea. When handled correctly, failure can provide the drive to keep going, a chance to identify what needs improving, and valuable experience that prepares you for future attempts.

First, failing can fuel motivation. A setback often forces people to stand up and try again rather than give up. Consider someone who sets an ambitious target: they should expect some obstacles along the way. When a setback occurs, it can act as a wake-up call to work harder and stay focused. For example, imagine a student who studies all night for an exam, hands it in feeling confident, and then discovers they did poorly. Instead of quitting, they choose to retake the test and study differently. Disappointing results do not always mean the end of a goal; often they simply mean a new start and a renewed effort.

Second, failure encourages reflection and improvement. The old saying that you learn from your mistakes is true. When things go wrong, people usually analyze what caused the problem and decide how to avoid repeating it. This process teaches better methods and clearer planning. By recognizing where they erred, individuals can correct weak points and make real progress. Improvement that comes after evaluating a failure is often more meaningful than success that comes easily.

Finally, failure builds useful experience. Without setbacks, people would miss out on lessons that strengthen them for later challenges. Overcoming difficulties provides stories and examples that can inspire both the person who failed and others watching. When someone reaches their goal after several failures, they have a powerful message to share about persistence and problem-solving. Hearing about those struggles can encourage others who are tempted to give up.

In conclusion, failure can be an important step toward success if it is used in the right way. Instead of seeing failure as final, treat it as a source of motivation, a prompt for improvement, and a way to gain experience. Approached like this, failure becomes a helpful part of the journey rather than a roadblock.

I have several abilities, but the one I enjoy most is skateboarding. It is a challenging skill: learning a trick can take hours, days, or even years. That difficulty is part of what makes skateboarding special. It has become part of my daily routine and helps me forget about stress and problems, which is why I love it so much. I use my board to get to the store, to a friend’s house, and sometimes even to school. Even though I often end up with scrapes, bruises, and other injuries, I still enjoy skateboarding because it has taught me important things like gaining confidence when I try new moves, getting back up after a fall, and learning from errors.

Skateboarding is more than a sport or a hobby to me — it feels like a way of life. It might not be the safest activity, but it remains one of my favorite skills, and I don’t think I will get tired of it anytime soon. When I was nine years old, many of my friends were already skating. I knew nothing about it at the time, so watching them practice felt exciting and different. Seeing them always motivated me, and eventually I decided I wanted to try it myself.

A few days after I first thought about it, I told my parents I wanted to learn to skateboard. My mother was worried and asked to think about it because she feared I might hurt myself. My father encouraged me to go ahead, and his support pushed me to try. The next day after school I asked my mom to take me to the nearest skate shop, and she agreed. Inside the shop I felt overwhelmed by all the parts — decks, wheels, bearings, and more — since I had never seen them before.

The person working there noticed I was new and asked if I needed help. I explained I had never stood on a skateboard, so he showed me the main parts: the deck, grip tape, trucks, wheels, and hardware. He also helped me choose the right pieces, and we began to put my first skateboard together. After we paid, he assembled it while I watched. It was already dark by the time we left, so I had to wait until the next day to try it.

When I came home from school the following afternoon, I dropped my backpack and rushed outside to test my new board. At first I only knew how to ride, but I immediately fell in love with the feeling of skating. Since that first day, I have practiced almost every day; if not daily, then at least every other day. Skateboarding has grown into something meaningful for me, teaching perseverance and giving me joy.

Sometimes I miss the mark and do not score three goals, but I remind myself that failing at least once is part of trying something difficult. Those mistakes teach me what I need to change and motivate me to work harder. Accepting failure helps you learn from errors and improves your chances of success next time.

Finally, it is valuable to try mastering different things instead of staying with one skill you already have. If you only focus on what you know, you will not become capable in other areas. Having several abilities gives you more options and makes you more flexible. Many people change their interests or pursue more than one goal at a time, so learning multiple skills is useful.

Summer is the longest school break of the year. While some educators suggest switching to year-round schooling with a shorter summer and a longer winter break, I disagree. I believe summer time should remain as it is because the weather can be very hot and students use these months for family trips, relaxation, or to find work.

First, extreme heat makes attending school uncomfortable and can lower students’ ability to learn. On many days temperatures climb very high, causing excessive sweating and headaches that make it hard to concentrate in class. When students are overheated, they become tired or irritable, and their schoolwork often suffers. Those who have to work in hot environments during the year will experience even greater difficulty performing tasks compared with working in milder weather. Overall, hot conditions reduce focus and energy, so shortening summer and forcing students back to school during this time would be unfair.

Second, summer provides a long period when students and families can travel or plan important activities together. Many families arrange vacations during these two months, whether a trip to the beach or visiting relatives in another country. Because there is no school, students can take longer trips without missing lessons or falling behind. In addition, some students use summer to find temporary jobs and earn money. With no classes to attend, they can concentrate on work and save for future needs. For many young people, the break is a valuable chance to spend time with family, gain work experience, and recharge.

In conclusion, summer should not be shortened by adopting year-round schooling. The season brings very hot weather that makes learning harder and gives students a useful stretch of time for travel, rest, and paid work. This long break is important for students’ well-being after a busy school year, and it should be kept.

Picture doing something you love so much that it never feels like work. My three main reasons for wanting this are: to get better, to build the right mindset, and to become a professional soccer player.

First, I want to improve. To do that I plan to train every day and ask coaches or more experienced players for guidance. When I make mistakes, I try to understand what went wrong so I can correct it the next time. Joining a team would help a lot because I could practice with players who are stronger than me or at my level. Playing matches and taking part in tournaments would also teach me a great deal, since I would learn from teammates and opponents in real competitions.

Second, having the right mindset is essential. I want to think and act like a professional: play without fear and treat the game seriously. Believing in myself is important — I must be convinced that I can reach the professional level. This attitude will help me face new challenges as I move forward, so keeping a strong, positive mindset is one of the most important parts of my plan.

Finally, becoming a professional is something I have dreamed of for as long as I can remember. Soccer is what I love to do, and I have worked toward this goal my whole life. Of course it can be tough sometimes and there is a risk of injury, but it also gives you the chance to meet many new people and to start a different kind of life. Another big attraction is that professionals earn good money, which is one reason many people aim for this career.

In conclusion, doing what you love makes it feel less like work. My three main reasons are to improve my skills, develop the right mindset, and ultimately play soccer professionally because it is my passion.

Imagination is a basic human capacity with an essential role: it supports our knowledge and inspires everything we create. Without imagination, people would struggle to develop understanding or come up with new ideas.

Imagination affects every part of daily life — work, family, school and more. Whenever someone plans how to carry out a task, they imagine the steps involved and foresee which knowledge and skills they will need. This mental planning helps people learn and adapt, which is why imagination has been important for human development over time. It allows us to face new situations and find different ways to solve problems.

Imagination is usually the first stage of any project, decision, or invention. When someone designs an object or plans a solution, they first form a mental picture of what is needed and how it should work. That initial image guides the use of skills and information to turn the idea into reality. In other words, ideas begin in the imagination, and knowledge and practice are used to realize them.

Knowledge itself depends on imagination. We use imaginative thinking to connect facts, see possibilities, and plan actions. Even if someone has technical skills in areas like math or science, those skills become useful only when applied to an imagined purpose or problem. Imagination gives direction to knowledge and makes creation possible.

In short, imagination is a central skill in everyday life. It helps people think, create, and use their abilities effectively in work, school, family life, and beyond. Without it, learning and invention would be much harder.

A successful career often starts when a student discovers a job they love while still young and studies toward it for many years. Children learn faster when they are younger, so it makes sense to introduce career ideas early. Parents often ask their kids what they want to be—doctor, teacher, dentist, police officer, or engineer—and schools encourage this by asking students to draw their future dream jobs. At a young age many students already imagine what they want to become, so choosing a career early can be useful.

Students also need enough time to prepare to succeed in their chosen field. Most professions require studying many subjects, and students sometimes do not earn enough credits and must retake classes. Some careers, like medicine, demand many years of training and are expensive. Future doctors must save money for their education or rely on government support or scholarships to afford tuition. In short, building a career requires time, money, and knowledge, so starting earlier gives students a better chance to do well.

Beginning career education young also lets students explore several options and later pick the best fit. When they try different subjects, they may discover a field they enjoy more than their first choice. Young people have more opportunities to test skills, gain experience, and improve their chances of finding well-paid work. Starting early gives them room to change direction if they learn their first plan is not right, and it can help them develop strengths for a higher-paying job.

Some people disagree and say children are too young to choose a future profession. They claim teenagers need more life experience before making such important decisions. Critics also worry that young students might simply copy a parent, uncle, or cousin without fully understanding the job. They argue that young people are not always responsible enough to decide their future career.

Despite these concerns, deciding on a career path at a young age has clear benefits. Early planning provides time to learn, to correct mistakes, and to gain the qualifications needed for success. A person who begins preparing for their chosen job early has a better chance of building a stable and rewarding future. Schools and families should encourage students to explore careers at an early age so they can make informed choices over time.

Finishing high school in three years and going straight to college can be a good option for many students. Some young people prefer to graduate earlier than their peers for different reasons. They may want to start earning money sooner to pay for college, spend more time with family, or take a break before college. In some cases, older students with family responsibilities—often from Hispanic communities—need to get a diploma quickly so they can find a steady job. If a student is prepared and meets the requirements, graduating a year early can make sense.

To finish high school in three years, students must work hard and meet all graduation requirements. For example, a 16-year-old in eleventh grade who lacks enough credits will not graduate on time. On the other hand, students who already have the needed credits or who take extra classes can leave early. Some students also balance jobs, family duties, or after-school activities, which makes planning more difficult. Schools usually offer extracurricular activities as well as chances to retake quizzes or get extra help from teachers.

Students who want to graduate early often need to do additional work. If a student struggles with a subject, staying after school for tutoring can help them earn the necessary credit. One downside is that working a job while finishing school can be exhausting. Teenagers who work after classes may become tired and find it harder to keep up with both school and their job. This extra pressure can make it difficult to complete all the requirements on time.

Many schools provide programs specifically designed for students who want to graduate in three years. These can include summer school or evening classes that let students earn credits faster. Such options make it easier to finish high school in a shorter time, but not every student can join these programs—some have work or family obligations during the summer. For students who cannot attend in-person programs, online courses offer another way to catch up or accelerate.

In conclusion, finishing high school in three years and starting college early can be beneficial, but it has both advantages and disadvantages. Programs like summer classes and online courses can help students graduate sooner, while working and extra study can cause fatigue and stress. Ultimately, whether a student succeeds depends on their effort and circumstances: if they do the required work, they can graduate early, but without that commitment it will be difficult.

Dear diary,

Today in English class my friends were saying that first impressions are almost impossible to change. I asked others what they thought, and I disagree with that idea. People can be going through a very hard time and not acting like themselves, they may treat different people differently, and sometimes a person’s behavior is caused by things they cannot control. One classmate suggested that someone might behave differently later, and I thought that was a good point.

My first reason is that someone could be in a bad moment and not feeling well. They might have just moved far away from home and left friends and family behind, or suffered a loss in the family, or feel very lonely. I know this myself because I have moved many times for my parents’ work. At one point they told me we might move every year and that changed how I felt; I became upset and didn’t want to go to school, I just wanted to have fun instead of studying. This year we haven’t moved, but my parents are looking at houses an hour away and we might move in January. Thinking about that makes me unhappy because Generic_School feels like home to me. The teachers here are helpful if you have problems inside or outside school, and they try to support you. I have made many friends and I really do not want to leave them — the people here are great.

Another point is that people do not always treat everyone the same. This happened to me once at a party. I went to meet a group of friends but they didn’t want to talk to me. I was confused until a girl told me they had been told something about me that wasn’t true. I explained to the girls that I hadn’t done what they thought, and I told them I have a twin sister who is different from me and who might have confused them. After I cleared things up, we fixed the problem and spent the rest of the night having fun together.

The third reason is that some children behave differently because of conditions they cannot control. My classmate told me about a boy he knows who is usually kind but sometimes becomes very angry and says hurtful things. He cannot fully control his emotions, and this is not his fault. When teachers explain what is happening to others, people understand better and stop blaming him.

So, after seeing all this, I still think first impressions are not always fair. Everybody makes mistakes or has bad moments, and we should give people a chance. Thank you for listening today!

Have a great day!

I disagree with the idea that first impressions cannot be changed. If you give people time and a second chance, they often can improve the way others see them instead of being judged forever for one mistake.

You would probably want the same forgiveness if you made a poor impression at a job meeting or on a date, so it is fair to give others the same chance to improve.

Second, a bad first impression can happen at an important work meeting. If you start badly, colleagues might think you are unprofessional or unprepared. However, with more time and another opportunity to perform, you can change that perception. Letting someone show their abilities again may lead people to say, “I was wrong about him; he’s much better than I first thought.”

Finally, personal situations also show why second chances matter. Imagine eating at your girlfriend’s parents’ house and accidentally making a bad impression. If the father quickly decides you are not the right person because of that moment, it would be hard to build a relationship. Being allowed to visit again and show a kinder, more respectful side can change his opinion.

In conclusion, people should be offered second chances to alter first impressions, so others can see who they truly are.

Thank you for giving me the chance to share my thoughts. From my point of view, life is short and many things happen quickly, but that does not mean first impressions cannot be altered. I disagree with the idea that a first impression is almost impossible to change. In my experience, impressions are often formed in a moment, yet they can be reshaped over time.

First, whether a first impression lasts depends on who the other person is and how much you get to know them. For example, if you meet someone you like, you may try hard to make a good first impression, and that image might stick for a while. But as you spend more time together and learn more about the person, your view can change. Time gives us more information and the chance to see a different side of someone.

Second, appearances and facial expressions can be misleading. I remember talking with a woman about a year ago who seemed angry when we first met. Her face looked upset, and I assumed she was mad. After we spent more time together, I realized she was not angry at all; she was just tired or thinking deeply. My first judgment proved to be wrong, and my impression of her changed completely.

Time is the most important factor here. It allows opinions to soften, misunderstandings to be cleared up, and memories to be reconsidered. A first impression may remain as the first image you had of someone, but it does not have to determine your long-term judgment.

In conclusion, yes — first impressions can change. You may never forget the initial moment, but with time and experience your opinion of someone can shift. We are always able to revise our views. Thank you.

I believe I understand why Thomas Jefferson wrote this message for his people. He wanted to encourage them to take responsibility for their own work and not waste time on small distractions. His goal was to help people achieve their dreams. At the time he wrote, many were afraid because they had recently been enslaved, and later Abraham Lincoln became president of the United States. That history helps show three reasons for Jefferson’s writing.

First, Jefferson wanted to observe whether people would follow his ideas. Many never consider what they could achieve in life because they spend too much time focused on others. If we keep wasting time, we will not reach our goals. Some are shy or afraid to pursue their dreams because others may criticize them or not believe in them. Often people fail simply because they do not try. If they made the effort, they might reach their ambitions.

Second, if we read Jefferson’s words carefully we can learn important lessons. Many of us lack the commitment needed to improve our lives. Some students attend school only because their parents send them there, and they do not see the opportunities that education can create. By paying attention to Jefferson’s message, we can learn to work harder and prepare for a better future. We should focus on our goals, study more, and aim for good grades so we can achieve what we want.

Third, although we live in freedom and have plenty of time, we often waste it on parties and going out with friends. If we always choose fun over our plans, we will not improve our lives. To succeed, we must be more committed to what we truly want for the future.

In conclusion, as young people we have the chance to do more and to set an example. With clear focus and the support of our families, we can reach our dreams. Jefferson’s words give us strength to keep going and not give up on what we hope to achieve.

If my teacher asked whether I prefer working alone or in a group, I would choose to work alone. Working by myself lets me come up with ideas that others might not think of. For instance, when I study alone I can sometimes get higher grades than when I share the task with a group. Group work often leads to unfinished assignments because classmates spend time talking or lose focus on what they should be doing. Some students prefer to work alone so they can hand in their assignments on time and avoid failing the class. Quiet or shy students also choose to work alone so they do not fall behind if they do not feel comfortable speaking up in a group.

Often students do not receive much real help from their classmates in group projects. It is common for a few people to do most of the work while others contribute very little. Some students simply sit and chat, check their phones, or play games instead of working, and they only discuss the task occasionally. While there are students who take responsibility and want to complete the assignment, it becomes clear that some prefer to socialize rather than work. For this reason, it is usually better for those who want to learn to work alone than to depend on a group.

Parents can also worry about the influence of friends when their child begins to fail a class. If a teacher calls to say a student’s grades have dropped, parents may blame the child’s peers and feel upset about the company their child keeps. In my view, working alone is the safer choice for many students. In the end, sometimes we must rely on our own effort to achieve what we want, rather than expecting help from others.

McDonald’s is a well-known fast-food chain where many employees earn only a small wage. If students could visit a place like this, they would see what can happen to people who do not focus on their education or who stop going to school. For that reason, I would pick a low-paid job as an example to show students the possible result of not taking their studies seriously.

A visit to a fast-food restaurant can change how students behave at school. They would observe workers who must move quickly and perform repetitive tasks, yet receive little pay. Seeing this everyday reality might discourage students from wasting time in class and encourage them to study harder so they can aim for better careers. Knowing what a difficult, low-paid job looks like could motivate many to work toward success instead of playing around.

It is also important to remember that some families cannot afford to support their children through further education. These young people often have no choice but to take tough, low-paying jobs. Students who do have access to schooling should understand that they have an opportunity many others do not. By appreciating their advantage, they might be more likely to use it to reach a stable, well-paid job later in life.

If students ignore their education, their parents’ efforts and money may be wasted. Parents often invest time and resources so their children can get a better future. If students do not pay attention and try, they may miss that chance and end up in low-paying work. Visiting a place like McDonald’s could remind them of this and prompt them to value their studies.

I would write a letter to McDonald’s asking for permission to bring students for a visit. Seeing employees’ hard work and low wages firsthand may help students decide to pay attention in class and make the most of their education so they do not end up in a job they do not want.

Should students accept a school district program that allows them to finish high school in three years instead of the usual four? I believe this option can be very beneficial for many learners.

Graduating a year early can be an excellent chance to move on from high school sooner. Not everyone enjoys high school, so completing it faster lets students pursue college or start working toward their goals earlier. Programs that include summer classes make it possible to earn the needed credits more quickly. This approach gives students extra time to prepare for university, explore possible majors, or begin earning money to support their families with expenses like rent and bills.

Of course, this path is not right for everyone. Some students may find the accelerated schedule too demanding and worry it will cut into their sleep or overall wellbeing. Others may feel that squeezing content into summer courses reduces the quality of their learning, since a typical school year covers about ten months and the shorter route concentrates many classes into a smaller period. There is also the risk of not completing all requirements if a student cannot keep up with the faster pace.

If I chose this program, I would take full advantage of the summer classes and other opportunities to gain extra credits needed for college applications. I would also start applying for scholarships and look for part-time work to support myself and my family. Planning ahead and staying organized would be important to make the most of the early graduation option.

In summary, people will have different opinions about this program, and it is not suitable for every student. Still, because it can help motivated students begin college or work earlier and move closer to their goals, I recommend that many students at least consider taking this offer. It could be a helpful step toward achieving future ambitions.

Some people rely on others to make choices for them, even about personal matters. The question asks whether individuals should decide for themselves or turn to experts and authorities when handling important life issues. While some argue that letting others choose removes stress and responsibility, I disagree with that view.

Many people feel uneasy about handing control to strangers or officials. It seems wrong to let someone who does not truly know you decide your future. Giving away the power to choose can lead to outcomes that do not match your values or needs, because others cannot fully understand your circumstances.

From my perspective, it is essential to learn how to make your own decisions. Life is personal, and we are the ones who must live with the results. Even if our choices sometimes lead to mistakes, those experiences teach us how to cope and grow. Asking for advice is acceptable—particularly from older or more experienced people—but that should remain just an opinion, not an order. We should not transfer decision-making authority to someone else and then expect them to manage our lives for us.

In conclusion, people ought to take responsibility for their own choices. No matter how challenging it may be, handling your decisions is part of living authentically and learning from the consequences. Therefore, I believe individuals should make their own decisions rather than rely on experts or authorities to do it for them.

People are debating whether technology has good or bad effects on our lives. Some argue that technology lets us do many tasks without meeting others face to face, while others blame it for reducing human contact. I believe technology brings mostly positive effects because it offers many benefits and greatly helps people in everyday life.

Today many of us lead busy lives with work, school, and other responsibilities. Teenagers often have heavy homework loads and sometimes work part-time, so free time is limited. Technology speeds up and simplifies many tasks. For example, if a student had to do a project without the internet, they might need to go to the library to find images, books, or other materials. That takes a lot of time and could cost money for travel or printing. With online resources and digital tools, schoolwork becomes faster and easier.

Some people worry that technology harms relationships. They say that families who eat together may all be looking at their phones and not talking, which weakens bonds. While this can happen, technology also makes it possible to keep in touch with friends and relatives who live far away. Apps like video calling and messaging let us see and hear each other instantly. If someone needs directions, services such as Google Maps help us find places quickly and avoid getting lost. In many everyday situations, technology provides practical help.

For me, technology is especially important for staying connected. My family lives in another country and some friends live in different states. I miss them, but I can call or video chat to celebrate birthdays or share news. On my birthday my family calls me using FaceTime and when it is my grandmother’s birthday I call her too. These small moments make us happy and closer, even when we are far apart. I also rely on maps to coordinate travel; for example, my mother uses Google Maps to pick up my father from work each day.

Overall, technology plays a major role in many areas of life. In science and medicine it has been crucial: doctors use advanced machines and tools that help diagnose and treat illnesses, saving lives. Of course, the effects depend on how people use technology. If it is used wisely, the benefits are clear.

In conclusion, technology has mainly positive effects on people’s lives. It helps us save time, stay connected across distances, and supports important work in medicine and education. How helpful it is depends on our choices, so we should use technology responsibly to get the best results.

Such choices help create a balance between what the body needs to work well and what it wants to eat.

The school menu is a good place to introduce these alternatives. It could include items students have never tried that are lower in fat than pizza or fried snacks. If children get used to a wider variety of foods now, they will be more likely to choose healthier options like salads or fish instead of only hamburgers or wings when they are older.

Many students look forward to summer vacation, but some teachers argue that the break is too long and that pupils become lazy or forget what they learned. I disagree with this view for several reasons.

First, summer provides time for students to do things they cannot fit into the school year. During the school term, homework and exams take up most evenings and weekends, so it is hard for young people to take on jobs or longer projects. With roughly three months off, students can work part-time, gain useful experience, or pursue interests that will help them later when applying for better jobs or further study. These activities teach responsibility and useful skills that a classroom year alone may not offer.

Second, students need a proper rest after many months of study. Constant work and the pressure of tests can be stressful, and young minds need a longer period to recover. Short one-week breaks are often not enough for real relaxation. Summer allows time to relax fully, spend more time with family, visit new places, or simply enjoy outdoor activities when the weather is pleasant. This break helps reduce burnout and returns students to school refreshed and ready to learn.

Finally, short breaks during the school year are rarely free of schoolwork. Teachers often assign projects or expect students to prepare for tests after a one-week holiday, so those breaks do not offer a true pause from school demands. In contrast, summer generally has fewer academic obligations, so students can enjoy a longer stretch without worrying about immediate assignments or exams.

Some people think having more frequent breaks during the year would be better, but they often overlook that these short holidays still involve school tasks. In short, students do not get the same mental rest during brief breaks as they do in summer.

In conclusion, summer vacation gives students a valuable long period to recharge and do things they cannot during the busy school year. For these reasons, the long summer break should be kept.

Imagine an old saying that claims honesty is the best policy. What would you think if someone used honesty in a harmful way — would you agree or disagree? I agree with this proverb because being truthful can have a deep effect on people’s lives. Honesty means telling the truth and it often helps form new friendships and strong connections.

I believe honesty is usually the best choice, although treating honesty carelessly can damage the trust others have in you. Losing someone’s trust is hard to recover. I remember a car accident where a seriously injured person lost the court case because the other driver was not honest about what happened. My father often tells me that honesty matters a lot. He has shared stories where his friends saw someone get robbed and, because a witness was truthful, the police were able to find and convict the thief. Even small acts of honesty can be helpful. That said, you should avoid using blunt honesty in ways that hurt someone’s feelings. Once, I was playing a game and the other team cheated and lied, and it upset some kids on my team. People can change how honest they are — a friend of mine used to lie often but gradually realized how important honesty is and became more truthful. I have also made friends simply by being honest. As these examples show, honesty can bring many benefits.

When you are consistently honest, people respect you. I have been in situations where my honesty made others treat me with more respect. Being open and truthful creates a positive atmosphere and helps build good relationships. On the other hand, when someone uses honesty to hurt or when someone is dishonest, it can feel like a deep betrayal — as though you have been struck by a train. One day I saw many police cars outside a neighbor’s house. I later learned she had been robbed a few months earlier, and a truthful witness had helped the police catch the criminal. This is another example of how important honesty is in solving problems and protecting others.

In conclusion, you should try to be honest in most situations. Your future actions and reputation will often benefit from the truth. Honesty encourages you to do the right thing, creates a better environment around you, and shows that you value yourself, which can be helpful in the long run. For all these reasons, I agree that honesty is the best policy.
