I believe working in a group is better because it brings many advantages. First, groups help people think more clearly and solve problems faster. Team members share ideas and information, which makes it easier to find solutions. When someone does research, they can use the internet or books and then explain what they learned to others. If a worker is sick or absent, others can cover their tasks so the work continues without delay. Although disagreements can happen, a professional team can discuss issues and find solutions together.

The second advantage is financial. When workers cooperate and do their jobs well, the company benefits and can pay better wages or offer more hours. Group work is often more efficient, so the business grows and may win new contracts or work with other companies and countries. This expansion creates more opportunities and income for both the company and its employees. 

In conclusion, I think group work is more useful for several reasons. It makes thinking and problem solving easier, allows colleagues to support each other when work is difficult, and helps companies and workers earn more through greater efficiency and business growth.

I agree with Emerson’s idea that you cannot grow unless you push beyond what you already know. Some people think growth happens naturally over time without effort, but I believe real progress requires trying new things and challenging yourself. If you want to reach your dreams, you must act and trust in your abilities.

You have to put effort into tasks that matter and give your best if you want to improve. From my own experience, I am growing because I work hard and encourage others to do the same. As students, when we develop ourselves, we can make a positive difference and make others proud. If we close our minds and refuse to try new things, then we will stay stuck and never improve.

In the long run, making an effort gives you something to rely on and opens the door to better options. Being organized and disciplined helps you move forward. It is also important to be true to yourself and not let others control your choices. The decisions you make are yours, and you must accept responsibility for them.

When you face a difficult choice, that is the moment to believe in yourself and decide whether you want to grow or remain where you are. Growing brings more chances for success, not only for you but often for the people around you as well. By improving, you can help others and create opportunities for your community.

Give your best to reach your goals. If you never try to grow, you limit what kind of person you will become. There are clear benefits to growth: you gain skills, become more adaptable, and can connect better with others. Emerson’s message is valuable—trying something beyond your current abilities is the way to progress. Take the risk and you might succeed.

Why it is not a good idea to save energy and resources at school?

Some students say conserving energy at school is a good idea because it reduces consumption and saves resources. I disagree. Many of us need the school's computers and internet to do homework. If we do not have computers at home, we must use school facilities, the library, or the classroom to finish assignments. But what happens if the computers are off because of energy saving measures?

We could lose points or get a bad grade for not handing work in on time. Imagine this happening for two hours one day — now imagine it happening for four school days. That would be a real problem for students who lack other resources. We would feel stressed and upset, and this could cause conflicts with our parents.

Some students can do work at home because their parents can pay for computers and internet. That is why those students may support saving energy at school. But many students do not have that option: their parents cannot afford internet, or there is only one parent who has to pay rent and bills, or there are many siblings sharing resources. There are many reasons families may not be able to pay for online access.

I do not think saving energy and resources at school is always a bad idea, but for some students the school is the only place where they can do homework safely and with confidence. If the school cuts energy for several days, it becomes hard to finish tasks on time. Even when computers are available, many students cannot use the same machines at once because everyone has different assignments and needs different software. This means some students will spend more time than others and fall behind.

Some people argue that students misuse the internet to check Facebook or play games, wasting the time that others could use. But you cannot judge all students by those who misuse it. Many use the internet for important reasons: homework, research, reading, and learning.

Another reason not to save energy in schools is the effect on heating and cooling. If the air conditioning or heating is turned off, extreme weather can make students and teachers uncomfortable or even sick. Also, without power we cannot charge phones, so students cannot contact their parents or call for help in an emergency. Energy is an important tool for communication and for handling urgent situations.

There are benefits to saving energy: the school could lower its electricity bill and use the money for other things, and we could do more outdoor activities. But if the school turns off power for several days, it would make learning much harder for many students. While some businesses can reduce energy use without serious harm, schools need reliable energy to support students’ education.

I agree with Emerson’s idea that trying to become someone different each day is one of the greatest achievements a person can have.

When you are true to yourself, you will still want to try new things and discover what you are capable of. Thinking about who you are makes life easier and more enjoyable. You are unique in this world, and only you can make the best choices for your life. Growing and changing is like receiving a valuable gift — something you must protect and nurture.

Constantly seeking new experiences teaches you things you did not know before. You will surprise yourself with abilities you did not expect to have, and that feeling — “I can do this” — makes you want to try more. Spontaneous experiences are often the most exciting and memorable. Experimenting helps you improve every day, and the skills you gain can help others. When we face situations where someone needs support, we can encourage them by showing that nothing is impossible. Many people lack self-belief because of bullying and cruel words. Those painful experiences make them feel worthless and often shy away from talking. That is why we must approach such people with kindness, respect, and patience. Speaking with love can heal; love is one of our strongest tools.

Too many people suffer from depression, anxiety, contempt, and racism, and some lose hope under the weight of insults and prejudice. We should not wait until someone reaches that breaking point. By working to stop bullying and racism, and by supporting others, we can change lives. Helping others also makes us better people. It gives us a new perspective, helps us find solutions, and proves that difficult things can be achieved when we decide to act with goodness and purpose.

It is time to take care of yourself and to listen to your heart. Improve yourself for your own sake, not to please others or to impress them. Do what makes you happy — follow your dreams, your plans, and your goals. Doing so will make you feel confident, interesting, and proud of your achievements. Pay attention to the people who speak kind, meaningful words to you; keep those words close. Throw away the harmful words that try to stop you, so they no longer affect your life. Be careful about telling everyone about your plans, because some people may be jealous and react with negativity. Share your hopes with those who truly care for you; they will celebrate your success with you.

Work on your individuality. When you do things by yourself, your work reflects your opinions, strategies, and solutions. I find that I can express all my ideas better when I work alone. Group work often forces us to combine ideas and choose only one approach, which can be limiting. For me, personal work allows my best ideas to grow.

Trying to become someone different — improving yourself every day — is a great achievement because it allows you to learn and do new things. It also pushes society to reject harmful behaviors and to be kinder. Children and young people should be free to follow their interests rather than only doing what others expect of them.

Yourself is precious; it defines your values and who you are. Surround yourself with people who help you become a better person and who stay with you in good and bad times. A true friend supports you, wants the best for you, and celebrates your successes. Someone who ignores your needs or does not care about what matters to you is not a real friend. Recognize who truly supports you.

Feeling comfortable with yourself brings real happiness. Many people struggle with body image and low self-esteem. When you are confident and believe in yourself, you feel happy in each moment. For me, the most important support comes from my faith. God loves me even before I was born, and that love gives me strength and peace.

Technology brings many benefits to people’s lives. It helps us prepare and complete tasks more quickly, reduces the time we spend on communication, and lowers the risk of losing important paperwork.

One clear advantage is how technology speeds up our work. Sending emails lets us share documents with colleagues or partners without having to travel or arrange meetings, which saves time and keeps things moving. By relying less on paper, we also cut waste and help the environment. For some people, communicating face-to-face can be stressful. Technology offers alternatives, such as emailing, that make it easier to discuss tasks or sensitive information without the pressure of in-person conversations. Another practical benefit is storage: we can keep projects, files, and presentations on flash drives, computers, or cloud services. Students, for example, often store essays and presentations on platforms like Office 365, so they do not need to worry about losing their work.

Some claim that technology harms our lives, but that view misses many advantages. Tools like PowerPoint make presenting information clearer and faster, and the internet gives us instant access to research and facts. Shopping online saves time because we do not have to go to stores, and the web also makes it simple to start a business: you can advertise vacancies, find workers, and manage operations digitally. Overall, technology improves efficiency in many areas of life.

In short, while it is not perfect, technology mostly improves how we work, communicate, and keep our important documents. It brings convenience, saves time, and opens new opportunities for both individuals and organizations.

When older students work with younger ones, it can lead to friendships and bring advantages for both groups.

Working together encourages friendship because the students must cooperate, listen, and talk to each other. Through these conversations they learn more about one another, such as personal interests or dislikes, which helps them get closer. Learning about someone else builds trust and makes it easier to become friends, and these new friendships can be especially helpful for the younger children.

Pairing older and younger students also helps the younger ones understand lessons better. They know someone is nearby to explain things if they are confused, so they feel more comfortable asking questions. Because the age gap is often only a few years, it is easier for younger students to share their opinions and for older students to understand their point of view. Also, rather than waiting for the teacher to finish with someone else, a younger student can get quick help from a peer who is already working on the same material.

Older students gain from this arrangement too. Teaching younger classmates teaches patience and the ability to stay calm when someone does not understand. It forces older students to use simpler words and clearer explanations, which improves their communication skills. They may also refresh their own knowledge when they explain a topic, so they learn while helping others.

In conclusion, pairing older students with younger ones creates friendships and supports learning for both sides. I believe it is important for students of different ages to work together because both benefit from the experience.

Students should not be allowed to bring cell phones to school because they are a major distraction. They often text whenever the teacher looks away, and when asked a question they might say they were not paying attention or ask the teacher to repeat it. Many pupils send messages to friends or partners about what they are doing instead of concentrating on their studies or planning for the future. While walking near the school, some text and fail to watch for traffic, which can cause accidents. Phones also encourage skipping class—students may not attend because a friend told them not to come. They spread gossip and talk about other people, passing rumors around. Because they spend so much time texting, they do not care about schoolwork and their grades suffer. In class they keep chatting and rarely focus on lessons. For these reasons, cell phones should not be allowed at school.

Even though some people have a negative attitude in their life and see all things as bad and do nothing for fear of making mistakes, people with a good attitude always see life another way. For example, when someone gives you very bad news but you take a good posture and say it is okay, everything will be good, and you keep a good attitude at school.

This is important because people believe they will pass and when they pass they feel so good, because this test was so hard, but they never surrendered.

When a person goes to the hospital and the doctor says they have an illness, instead of thinking all the negative things like "I will never be the same person" or "I will die," they decide, "okay, it is a little illness, it will pass in some days, my life will be a little different, but everything will be good."

Seeing life in a positive way is thinking that all things are possible. Always do not care how big the problem is; be happy. Watch the most terror situation like the best way possible and do not be worried for all the things that happen in your life. Be as happy as you can and see the biggest problem as the smallest.

When people choose to adopt a positive attitude, their lives tend to improve. Even though some individuals focus on the negative and expect everything to go wrong, those who keep an optimistic outlook view situations differently. For example, if someone tells you very bad news, a person with a positive mindset might respond calmly and say, "It will be okay," instead of becoming completely discouraged. This same hopeful approach is useful at school and in other parts of life.

If people stayed positive in most areas of their lives and worried less, they would be happier overall. Imagine you face a difficult test at school and feel you cannot pass. If you keep a constructive attitude, a friend or family member may encourage you and tell you that you will succeed. That encouragement matters because believing you can pass increases your chances, and when you do succeed you feel proud, especially after working hard and refusing to give up.

The same idea applies to health problems. If a doctor diagnoses an illness, it is easy to jump to the worst conclusions and think life will never be the same. But someone who chooses optimism might decide that the illness is manageable, that it can get better after treatment, and that life will continue with some adjustments. This calm, realistic hope makes dealing with illness less frightening.

Seeing life through a positive lens means believing many things are possible and not letting problems become overwhelming. Even in scary situations, try to wait for the best outcome and avoid constant worry. By aiming to be as happy as you can and treating big problems as manageable, life becomes easier to enjoy and challenges become less threatening.

I agree with Emerson’s idea that our choices and actions should be guided by experience. Experience gives us the support and confidence to try new things. When you have practiced and learned from what you’ve done before, you are more likely to move forward, take on responsibilities, and improve your position. In short, experience helps you grow and find better opportunities.

At the same time, experience does not appear by itself. You become ready for bigger challenges only after preparation and practice. If someone has not read, practiced, or learned the basics, they will struggle to advance. That is why it is important to work on your skills, ask questions, and get advice from teachers or supervisors. Their guidance helps you understand what you do not yet know and speeds up your learning.

Many people fail to make progress because they do not put in the necessary effort to gain experience. They expect immediate success without the practice needed to reach it. On the other hand, those who train, prepare, and learn step by step find it easier to succeed. Experience makes tasks simpler and opens the door to better positions and clearer goals.

In conclusion, I believe decisions should be based on experience, but only after you have built that experience through hard work and learning. Being prepared and willing to practice will make your experience meaningful, help you grow, and allow you to face new challenges with confidence.

The statement "Unless you try to do something beyond what you have already mastered, you will never grow" is something I disagree with. I believe people can develop and improve even after making mistakes because everyone deserves another chance to learn and grow.

First, I will explain my idea with a simple example from school. Imagine a group of students working on a class assignment. Each student may have a different idea, but one person is chosen as the leader. The group prepares the project, and when it is almost finished, they decide to present it. The leader sees the result and says it is not good enough or incomplete, so they must discuss the problems again and continue improving the work. No one in the group should say, "I cannot do this" or "I won’t try again." Instead, they keep working until the project meets their standards. This shows that making a mistake or failing once does not stop a person from growing; they can revise their work and try again.

Second, everyone deserves multiple chances to improve, not only in school but in life. If you make a mistake, it does not mean you must repeat it forever. People can learn from errors and become better for themselves, their class, and their community. For example, consider someone who has committed a crime but wants to change and get an education. I think this person should be allowed the opportunity to study and rehabilitate, because giving second chances helps people rebuild their lives. Some people will disagree and say that criminals do not deserve another chance. In my opinion, they should, because being punished does not remove the possibility of personal growth. If a person wants to become better, education and support can help them change.

I understand that my view may upset some people. They might feel that certain actions are too serious for forgiveness. Still, I believe that if we imagine ourselves in the same situation, we would want the chance to improve. Helping others grow also makes the world a little better.

In conclusion, people often have second or even third chances to grow. We should think about ourselves and others, and give opportunities to learn and improve. I come from a country with few opportunities, but my goal is to become a better person today and in the future. Everyone should be allowed to try again and prepare for a better life.

Technology can be both helpful and harmful.

On the positive side, many people treat technology like a friend because it makes daily life easier. It allows us to stay in touch with family and friends who live far away. It also works as a useful tool for learning and shopping: you can find books, research information, or buy things that you might otherwise have to go to a store to get. Technology helps job seekers search and apply online, and students can get information from colleges without visiting in person. Online shopping saves time and travel, and digital games or apps can help relax your mind when you are stressed. In some cases, technology even supports practical problems at home, like finding advice for repairs or finding services to fix a building.

On the negative side, technology often shows only its good side while hiding risks. Fake websites and profiles can look safe, but you do not always know who made them or why. Criminals and extremist groups can use the internet to find and influence young people, especially if parents are not watching what their children do online. People can spend too much time on social media or shopping sites, and some users exploit this by selling fake products or tricking others into paying for things that do not exist.

In the end, technology has two sides — good and bad — and which one you meet depends on how you use it and where you go online.

I disagree with the idea that first impressions can never be changed. Although some people hold on to their initial judgments and believe they are certain, those impressions can and often should be re-evaluated. It is important to check whether your first reaction is based on facts or on assumptions before you act on it.

For example, once while I was at home exercising I suddenly became convinced that my girlfriend was cheating on me with my best friend. That thought made me very upset. When you have a negative impression of someone, you need to be careful about how you respond. Acting immediately on a strong but unconfirmed feeling can create problems. I called my girlfriend and we talked for a long time, but I did not know the best way to tell her about my suspicions. I wanted to change my first impression, yet my thoughts were confused because I feared the consequences if I accused her wrongly.

In the end I realized that my initial belief was not necessarily true. Many first impressions come from uncertainty or incomplete information, so they can be mistaken. My experience taught me that impressions may change after you gather more facts or discuss the situation calmly. Sometimes the best choice is to keep your thoughts to yourself and wait; time and communication will reveal whether your impression was correct. Now I tend to hold back my first reactions and give myself time to think, which helps me revise and correct those early judgments.

I do not support changing our school to a four-day week. Although some businesses have found success with a shorter workweek, this model would cause several problems for students and families. Longer school days would reduce family time, increase homework and tiredness, create supervision issues for younger pupils, and add stress that hurts learning.

First, longer school days mean less time with family and less free time after class. If we spend more hours at school, we will come home exhausted and have fewer opportunities to relax, play, or be with our parents and siblings. Children enjoy going out with friends after school, and that time helps them recharge. If schools try to limit that time because students already study many hours, pupils will feel frustrated and unhappy.

Second, a four-day week would probably bring more homework and extra lessons to cover the same material. Students might finish a long day at school only to face a heavy amount of homework, leaving little time to eat, rest, or talk to family. Staying too long in one place is difficult for many children and makes learning feel boring and tiring. Some students might use their phones or watch videos when they are free, but this is not a healthy solution for everyone.

Third, there are family and supervision concerns. Many students are under 18 and need parents to help them get to and from the bus or watch after them at home. If school days are longer, parents may have to change their work schedules to care for their children. Emergencies at school can also be harder for working parents. On the other hand, some students use a free weekday to work and earn money, learn responsibility, and speak with different people. While this is positive for those students, it can also distract others from their studies if they prefer earning money to attending school.

Fourth, spending more time at school can be stressful. Even if students can focus for longer, doing so every day can cause mental fatigue and boredom. This reduces the desire to learn new subjects or languages outside school. Technology like computers and phones helps education, but too much screen time can harm eyes and concentration. Students often use devices for many tasks, but overuse can be dangerous for health and attention.

In conclusion, school is not the only place where students learn about life, but it should give ideas and structure. A four-day school week is not the same as a four-day workweek for adults. For these reasons, I do not think our school should adopt this model. It would create more problems than benefits for students and families.

I believe taking summer classes to finish high school in three years is a good idea. Finishing earlier lets students start working or do other things sooner. For example, they could get a job and earn money, help their family at home, or buy things they need like a car or clothes. These practical benefits make a shorter high school period attractive.

Some students arrive in the United States at 15 or 16 and are placed in ninth grade. If these students finish high school in three years, they will be about 18 and able to enter the workforce earlier than if they stayed four years and graduated later. However, this situation can be different for Hispanic students who are still learning English. Even if they graduate at 18, they might not have strong enough English skills to find good work right away.

For many American students whose English is already fluent, finishing in three years can be easier and more useful. They do not face the same language barrier, so being younger when they graduate helps them find jobs and earn money sooner.

Finishing one year early can be challenging academically and personally, but I think it is a worthwhile option for students who are 18 to 20 years old and ready for the challenge. If my school offered the choice, I would pick the three-year plan because it fits my age and goals better.

You can learn how to work as a team because in group work you have to make sure you are being nice to your teammates and you must listen to everyone else's point of view. In group work you learn how to respect others.

Working with a group has more benefits than working alone because if you have a big project to do and your teacher allows you to work as a group but you choose not to join any group and decide to work alone, it will be hard for you to complete the project on time. The people who join the group can easily complete the project before you because they can help each other. This is the biggest benefit of working with a group.

In group work all the members of the group have to do equal work, and this way they can do their part of the project very easily. If they work alone they are not able to work that well because they have no one else to give them advice or any kind of help. Therefore group work is always a benefit.

Group work always gives you benefits.

Is working in a group beneficial? I believe that working with others is better than working alone. Groups can complete tasks more quickly than one person can. In a group you must be polite to teammates and listen to their ideas, which helps you learn to respect other people’s views.

Group work brings more advantages than working by yourself, especially for large projects. If your teacher allows group work but you choose to work alone, it can be very difficult to finish everything on time. Those who work together can divide the tasks and support each other, so they often complete the project faster. This practical benefit is one of the main reasons to choose group work.

When a team divides the work fairly, each member can focus on a smaller part and do it well. A person working alone may struggle because they do not have anyone to ask for feedback or help. Group members can give advice, share knowledge, and solve problems together, which improves the final result. For these reasons, group work is usually more effective.

Some people think group work should not be allowed, but I still feel it is the best way to study. Teamwork teaches responsibility because everyone must do their share. It also gives a chance to exchange ideas and improve the quality of the project, which can lead to better grades. Overall, group work has many clear benefits.

Winston Churchill once said that failure is part of success and we should not lose our enthusiasm because of small setbacks or a single defeat. I agree with his view because making mistakes helps us grow and become better at what we do.

When we fail, we learn from our errors and start to improve our skills. Each attempt teaches us something new about the problem and about ourselves. By trying again and again, we gain experience and gradually reduce the same mistakes. Over time, these lessons make it easier to solve similar problems in the future.

Persistence is important. If you keep working hard on something you do not yet understand, you will often discover new ways to fix the issue. Failure does not mean you cannot find a solution; it usually means there is an aspect you have not noticed or a different approach you have not tried. Recognizing that helps you change direction and continue progressing.

Trying repeatedly also builds confidence and teaches problem-solving. As you explore different options, you learn what works and what does not. This process not only benefits you but can also help others; sharing what you have learned or working with someone else can lead to better solutions, because two people can see things in different ways.

In conclusion, success often requires passing through many mistakes. By exploring, learning from failure, and continuing to try, you can find solutions and grow. Staying enthusiastic and persistent is the key to eventual success.

Many high school students try hard to get good grades, and I think choosing a career path early can be a positive step. Making decisions about a future profession while still young helps students learn more about their interests and prepares them for the next stages of life.

One reason I support early career commitment is that it gives students time to explore a field. When teenagers focus on a particular area, they can take related classes and see what the work is really like. This experience shows whether the career fits their skills and personality. If it does not, they still have time to change direction before they invest too much in one path.

A second reason is that concentrating on a chosen career often improves school performance. Students who take specialized or advanced courses tend to learn more quickly because the material matches their goals. Passing these classes shows they understand the subject and can help them meet the requirements for university programs. In this way, early focus can make the transition to higher education smoother.

A third reason is practical preparation for adult life. Studying in a targeted way and taking challenging subjects helps students build habits like hard work and discipline. These qualities are useful both in college and in the job market. If students graduate having already covered important topics for their chosen field, they are more likely to find good jobs and feel satisfied with their efforts.

In conclusion, deciding on a career at a younger age can be helpful. It allows students to test their interests, improve their academic success, and get ready for higher education and work. While not every young person must make a final choice immediately, having a clear direction during high school can give many students valuable advantages for the future.

I believe the best choice for me is to take classes online from home.

My main reason is that online learning fits better with other responsibilities. If you have a job, it can be hard to attend face-to-face lessons. Also, some students do not have transport or cannot travel to another place for lessons, so studying from home is more convenient.

It is not always easy — online learning needs effort and self-discipline, and sometimes a teacher is not there to explain things immediately. Even so, with determination and sacrifice you can complete the work and pass the classes.

For all these reasons, my recommendation is to choose classes from home by online methods. This option is more flexible and convenient for time, transport, and personal responsibilities, and it helps students manage their studies better.

I agree with Winston Churchill’s view that success often comes through repeated failures while keeping your enthusiasm. Failure is not the end; it is part of the path that teaches you and gives you strength to continue. If you face setbacks but remain hopeful and determined, you increase your chances of reaching your goals.

Churchill’s idea reminds us that persistence matters more than never making mistakes. Many people give up after one or two failures because they lose confidence or stop trying. But those who accept failures as lessons and keep their energy and belief—whether in God, themselves, or both—can recover and move forward. A strong faith or inner conviction helps some people stay motivated through hard times.

Following good habits and rules also helps when you are trying to succeed. Discipline and a clear plan make you less likely to be defeated by difficulties. If you practice, learn from your errors, and keep a steady attitude, each failure becomes a step closer to success. The important point is not to let disappointment destroy your enthusiasm.

I believe this idea is very practical. When you battle against failure and do not lose your courage, you will eventually achieve something worth being proud of. Not everyone reaches success because some people are not willing to face life’s challenges or change their thinking. Those who do not follow a correct path or keep a positive mindset often remain stuck.

In short, success and failure are connected. You may fall many times, but rising each time with the same eagerness leads to real achievement. I agree with Winston Churchill: moving from failure to failure without losing enthusiasm is a true recipe for success.

I believe students should not be forced to take elective classes because those courses are often not essential and can waste students’ time. Since electives are usually optional for graduation, many students do not take them seriously. They may not put in effort, earn failing grades, and see their GPA drop. When students know a course is not required, they may skip it or do poorly, which can cause trouble later.

Electives can distract students from more important required classes. Time spent on electives could instead be used to study subjects that count toward graduation or improve academic performance in core courses. Some students want to finish their required credits quickly, and being obliged to take electives slows that process down. Schools should let students choose whether to take electives so those who prefer to focus on required credits can do so.

Because elective classes are not needed to graduate, students often treat them casually. They have other classes that directly affect their diploma, so they prioritize those. As a result, they may not complete assignments or prepare for exams in electives. This behavior can lead to failing marks, which lower overall grades and may hurt a student’s chances when applying to college or scholarships.

Many students also find certain electives boring or irrelevant to their interests. Not every student enjoys music, art, or drama; some prefer sports or more academic subjects. If a student dislikes a particular elective, they might try to avoid it, skip classes, or do minimal work. That avoidance can create problems—missed credits, disciplinary issues, or a weaker transcript—that affect future plans, such as college admission or eligibility for some jobs.

In conclusion, elective classes should not be compulsory because they are often seen as unimportant and students may not take them seriously. Allowing electives to be optional would let students concentrate on required coursework, finish their credits faster if they wish, and avoid the negative consequences of failing or skipping classes they do not care about. Schools should give students the choice to take electives rather than forcing these courses on everyone.

Some companies have moved to a schedule with ten-hour workdays and fewer workdays per week. This change can be good for employees because they earn more and spend fewer days commuting. However, schools should not copy this business model because students would not attend regularly and would miss important learning.

Schools cannot follow the same pattern as businesses. Many students would stop coming to class every day and might only show up two days a week. If that happens, they would miss most lessons and fall behind on the curriculum. Education requires consistent attendance so students can learn step by step; working long shifts would take up too much time and leave no space for regular schooling.

Another reason schools should avoid this idea is that students’ grades would suffer. Missing classes makes it hard to understand what teachers are teaching and to complete assignments. Students who attend infrequently will have weaker grades and less understanding of the material. They will also miss class activities and discussions that help them learn.

Working longer days can be a benefit for young people because it brings more income, but it should not replace attending school. A better option is to work after school or on weekends so students can keep up with their studies, do homework, pay attention in class, and show respect for teachers. In conclusion, teachers and schools want students to graduate and succeed, so students need to attend school regularly and can take jobs outside school hours.

I disagree with this idea because a first impression does not always show a person's true character. People can behave differently later, and there are many reasons why someone might seem unfriendly at first: they may be shy or have had painful experiences with others before.

For instance, if a person sees someone in need but does not help, others might think they did not care. Often it is not unwillingness but nervousness or a quiet nature that stops them from acting. They may worry about getting involved or have learned to keep their distance because of past hurt.

Small moments can be misread too. One person may greet someone warmly but receive a curt reply. If this happens more than once, people may assume that the replied person is not kind. Later, when they meet again and the person is friendly, others realise the earlier reaction was not typical. Because first encounters can be misleading, it is better to wait and see how someone behaves over time.

I speak in favor of Thomas Jefferson because he was a man of action, not someone who stayed idle. He wanted to know how long tasks would take and what tools or materials were needed to complete them. He expected people to work honestly and not fight, steal, or take money from others. Jefferson believed that education mattered: those who finished school could find better jobs and earn more, while people without schooling tended to get lower pay.

Jefferson served the United States both in military roles and as a national leader. He was involved in the American struggle and worked to support the country in times of conflict. He helped organize people and provided assistance that improved citizens’ lives. In his view, expanding the nation and making it stronger on the world stage were important goals, and his actions aimed to increase America’s power and influence.

He also used speeches to explain his purposes to the public. Jefferson spoke about what he thought was good for the people, praised virtues, and warned against harmful behavior. Many people admired him and followed his ideas, but some disagreed strongly and even plotted against him. His positions and words sometimes made him a target of harsh criticism.

From a young age Jefferson read widely, forming his ideas and plans through study. He had friends and allies who supported his decisions and helped him carry out his aims. Overall, Jefferson played a significant role in serving America by encouraging work and education, strengthening the nation, and communicating his vision to the public.

Tomas Jefferson urged people to resolve not to be idle, suggesting that if we keep working, we will accomplish a great deal. I understand his message as a call to make a firm decision to stay active and productive, because constant effort often leads to surprising results.

There are essentially two kinds of people when it comes to this idea: those who accept Jefferson’s advice and those who do not. Some believe it is unnecessary to be busy all the time; they prefer to act only when something becomes urgent. Others think you should put effort into what matters to you and only at the right moments. I strongly agree with Jefferson’s view. Regular effort builds momentum and produces outcomes that would not appear if we waited for perfect conditions.

Negative thinking often stops people from working toward their dreams. When someone doubts their chances of success, they may become passive and give themselves permission to be idle. In many cases, people look for reasons to avoid effort — excuses that justify inactivity rather than confronting the work needed.

For me, the lesson is clear: keep doing something every day to move forward. Small, steady actions add up and lead to meaningful achievements. By refusing idleness and maintaining a steady effort, we increase our chances of reaching our goals and becoming the successful people we hope to be. I fully agree with Jefferson’s advice and believe that persistence is the key to real progress.

Many people think that working alone is more beneficial because students learn more when they do tasks by themselves. In group projects the work is often split, and each student does only one part. As a result, no one learns the whole subject in detail. When someone works alone, they must handle every part of the task and so they understand everything more completely.

Group work also has clear advantages. It is usually faster and easier because each person takes a portion of the work. If one student does not understand something, others can explain it, and this helps everyone learn. For these reasons many students prefer group work. However, a common problem in groups is that sometimes a member does not contribute, leaving the rest to finish the work.

Personally, I prefer to work alone because I learn and understand more. When I do a task by myself, I need to collect all the information, solve all the examples, and prepare the full explanation. This process forces me to study more and gain a deeper understanding. Still, it is important to know how to work both alone and in a team, since in the future people will sometimes need to work by themselves and sometimes with others.

Both ways have useful points, but I think working alone is better, especially at the beginning. For teachers, individual work is also helpful because it shows how each student thinks and works. Not all students perform the same way in group settings, so individual tasks allow teachers to see each student’s real abilities. Overall, I believe students learn more when they work alone, though they should also learn to cooperate with others.

Yes, preparing for the future while still a student is a very good idea because it helps you decide what you want to do later in life. If young people think early about their goals, they can choose a career that fits them and take the right steps, such as studying for university or getting practical experience. By doing this, they will be more ready for adult responsibilities: finding a job, earning money, and supporting their family or partner when needed. Parents often show useful examples and guide their children, so listening to them can help you avoid mistakes and make better choices.

In many places, students who plan ahead are more prepared when they start a family or change their lives. Studying opens more opportunities and helps you become a stronger, more responsible person. If you work hard at school, earn good grades, and develop skills like giving presentations, you increase your chances of getting a better job and possibly becoming a leader or manager later. That is why focusing on your studies and career is important—you will be able to help friends and family and build a stable future.

On the other hand, many people fail to reach their goals because they were not ready when chances appeared. Some do not appreciate opportunities and find it hard to catch up later. If it becomes too late for formal education, there are still practical jobs you can start with, such as construction, truck driving, or working as a cashier. These paths can still provide income and experience, but preparing earlier makes it easier to aim for higher positions.

For example, if you study seriously now, you will be ready for adult responsibilities and more likely to get office jobs or other careers you want. Parents can support and encourage you by watching your progress and reminding you to study. With preparation, you will have more choices in life and will not be able to say that your parents did not help your future.

My advice is to prepare and work hard for your goals. Studying now gives you a better life and makes you a good role model for your future children. When they grow up, they will see the example you set and try to follow it. Believe in yourself, work hard, and stay focused—no one can take away your chances if you keep trying.

I believe first impressions are not always permanent. For example, when I first met my girlfriend I thought she was very cheerful. After spending more time with her, I realized she was not as happy as she seemed at the beginning, and my view of her changed.

Many people behave differently when they meet someone new. If you go to a job interview, you may smile and act friendly so the employer will hire you, even if you are feeling sad inside. Later, after they have worked with you for a while, they might see the real side of your personality and their first impression will change.

The same happens in other situations, like starting a new school. At first, students often try to look cool or say things they think others like so they will fit in. With time, classmates discover who they really are and their initial opinion can be different.

Some people argue that in-person school is better, and they have reasons, but I think online classes are a better option. Taking classes from home has downsides, but it also brings many advantages that make it worth trying.

First, online learning lets you stay at home, so you do not need to get up very early or ride a bus. You can avoid going into a school building and sitting next to people you might not want to see. At home you can eat whatever you prefer at any time, instead of having to accept the school lunch. You also have more control over your daily routine and can organize your time the way that suits you best.

Another advantage is that tests can feel easier when you study online because you can quickly search the internet for information. This makes it simpler to find answers and learn in a way that helps you pass. Being at home can reduce stress from strict school rules, too; there are fewer chances to get in trouble for small things.

In a traditional school, you have to follow many rules: be on time for class, sit in assigned seats, and attend all lessons. If you are late or miss classes often, schools sometimes put you in in-school suspension (ISS), where you sit quietly without a phone or talking to others. They will notify your parents if you skip school, and most parents will be upset if they thought you were attending when you were not.

Discipline at school can become more serious. Teachers can call security if a student disrespects them, and security officers will come to handle the situation. If students fight, it can lead to major consequences: medical help, the principal, the police, and calls to parents. The other student’s parents may press charges. Such incidents leave a record that can damage your reputation and make it harder to get into college.

The risks grow worse if a student uses or sells drugs at school. That can lead to trouble with the police, expulsion, or even jail, depending on the law and how old the student is. Being removed from your school would mean leaving friends behind and starting over at a new place, which would be very upsetting.

For these reasons, I believe online classes are a good choice and worth trying as an experiment. They reduce many of the problems that happen in physical schools and give students more freedom and safety.

As young people grow up, they begin to form opinions about others. Many say that first impressions are fixed and cannot be altered. I disagree. I believe that it is possible to change the impression people have of you by showing different behavior over time.

Often people judge others by their facial expression or the way they act at first meeting. If you look sad, tired, or unfriendly, others may think you are rude or uninterested. But these reactions can be corrected. By smiling more, speaking kindly, and showing respect, you can give others a new, more positive view of you. Small changes in how you present yourself can change what people think.

This is especially important in places like work or school. If you want a job that requires friendliness and a positive attitude, you may need to adjust your behavior. Employers and colleagues notice how you act, so demonstrating that you are polite and cooperative can replace a bad first impression. People are likely to treat you better when they believe you are respectful and pleasant.

Personality is often what people notice first, but that does not mean it is fixed. You can prove to others that you are not the person they first assumed. Showing consistent, friendly actions helps others revise their initial opinion. In conclusion, first impressions are not impossible to change; with effort and positive behavior, you can show people the real you and improve how they see you.

I agree with Ralph Waldo Emerson because his ideas encourage people to grow by thinking and acting for themselves. Even if some people feel afraid to try new things or to speak up, Emerson’s message can help them form their own opinions. When people share their views and listen to others, they can understand different perspectives and learn how to agree or disagree respectfully.

Not everyone will accept the same opinion, and that is normal. Some people will agree with Emerson and some will not. Still, agreeing with an idea does not mean you stop learning; instead, agreement often comes from experience and reflection. A person may not be ready to give an opinion at first, but after trying and seeing the results, they can understand better and may choose to agree. Experience helps people grow and make stronger choices.

Emerson’s thoughts become more useful when he and others explain them and show how they work in real life. If he shares his ideas and people try them, more people will understand and might accept them. This process of sharing and trying brings growth. If people stay inactive or afraid, they will not develop. By practicing ideas and communicating with others, people can rise instead of staying down.

In the end, agreeing with Emerson means supporting independence and learning from experience. People can help each other to explore ideas and to do what they want. When we talk, try, and support one another, we all have the chance to grow and improve.

My view on switching to a four-day school week is mixed, but I am mostly against a change that makes school days longer. Having an extra day off could be good for students and teachers. That free day could be used to sleep more, study topics we do not have time for, spend time with family, or work on personal interests and self-improvement. I can see many positive things about getting one more day each week.

However, the downside worries me. To keep the same number of lessons, school days would probably be extended by about two hours. Right now we already spend around seven hours at school, which feels long. Most students wake up very early, around 5:30 or 6:00 a.m., prepare for the day, and then stay at school for those seven hours. Adding two extra hours would make the days even more tiring and leave less time for sleep, family, or other activities.

If school becomes longer, I would lose much of the free time I currently enjoy during the week. Because of that loss, I do not support a four-day week that lengthens each school day. We should think carefully about what will really help students before making this change.

Many schools permit the use of cell phones in class for learning because they want students to access different ways of studying. When used properly, phones can support lessons and help students prepare for life outside school. At the same time, teachers worry that students might use phones for non-educational activities if they are not guided.

Some teachers try to show students how to use phones responsibly. They give tasks that involve research, creating documents, or finding events and resources related to the subject. Other teachers use phone apps to run online quizzes or exams so students can practice and be assessed quickly.

Policies about cell phones differ between schools. Some schools allow phones under certain rules, while others ban them completely. These rules are meant to prevent distraction and maintain order during class. There are also programs and organizations that help schools design lessons which include phones in meaningful ways, so students learn useful skills without losing focus on traditional study methods.

In conclusion, there are many ways to teach with cell phones, but it is important for teachers to explain why they are using them and how students should behave. I have heard teachers ask students what else a phone can do besides making calls, and many students cannot answer. Phones can be powerful tools to improve learning and personal growth, but students must avoid wasting time on them. Reading books and using computers remain valuable, yet exploring new technology is also important for a balanced education.

I believe a positive attitude is the key to success in life. When you keep a hopeful and constructive outlook, you open yourself to more opportunities and improve your chances of reaching your goals. A positive mindset affects many parts of life — personal matters, work, and family — and it starts with how you view yourself.

Having a positive attitude leads to greater success both personally and professionally. For example, when you show a friendly and optimistic face to others, you can lift their mood too. If someone is having a bad day, your smile or encouraging words may help them feel better and think differently about their problems. By sharing positivity, you make it easier for other people to move forward and improve their lives, and this creates a better atmosphere around you every day.

In the workplace, a positive attitude also makes a big difference. If you treat your colleagues kindly and stay upbeat, you build stronger relationships with your team. This often leads to more trust, smoother cooperation, and better results. Over time, a productive and friendly environment can bring more opportunities, such as promotions or increased responsibilities. A positive person is more likely to be noticed and rewarded because they contribute to a healthier workplace.

Positivity is especially important within families. Good family relationships give emotional support and help us become better people. For instance, when my father died, my family supported me through a very difficult time and helped me overcome depression. Their care and a positive attitude helped me survive that painful period. Strong family bonds can be your best resource for a secure and hopeful future.

In conclusion, I think having a positive attitude leads to success in life. It affects how people respond to you, improves your professional and personal relationships, and helps you face hard times without losing hope. Even when things are difficult, try to keep a positive outlook, because your actions and attitude bring rewards over time. If you remain positive with others, you will increase your chances of success.

I believe older children should not be paired with younger ones because they often set a bad example, behave unsafely around little kids, and show a lack of respect.

When older kids act badly, younger children may copy them. This can lead to dangerous situations. For example, an older friend might perform a skateboard trick that looks easy. A younger child, trying to imitate it without the skill, could fall and seriously hurt themselves. My brother once watched his friend try a skateboard trick; I copied it, fell, and broke my arm. That showed how risky it can be when younger children follow older ones.

Another worry is that older kids might use drugs or smoke. If a young child sees someone smoking nearby, they could breathe in the smoke or be influenced to try it later. My friend’s brother smoked while we were together; we warned him that smoking is harmful, but he didn’t stop. That example is unsafe and confusing for younger children.

Respect is also important. Older kids should treat little ones politely so they learn to be respectful in return. If older children are rude, younger children may copy that behavior. One of my friend’s brothers was disrespectful to us, and we responded in the same way.

For these reasons—poor examples, unsafe behavior, and a lack of respect—I think older children should not be placed around younger ones unless they are responsible and respectful. If they were responsible and behaved well, it could be okay.

I believe students would gain a lot from being able to join classes from home through online lessons or video conferencing. Learning remotely gives students extra time because they do not have to travel to school by walking or taking a bus. That saved time can be used for studying or part-time work. Many students also find it easier to concentrate at home where there are fewer unrelated conversations or disruptions than in a busy classroom.

Online classes also allow students to choose when to start lessons, which helps those who have jobs or other responsibilities. On cold or bad-weather days, students can continue learning without leaving the house. This flexibility can encourage greater responsibility, though how well a student does depends on their personal habits and motivation.

For some learners, studying at home lowers stress. They can take short breaks, have a snack, and work in a comfortable space, which can help them use their mental energy better. Parents can more easily see whether their child is doing assignments and offer support when needed. Personally, I find it simpler to finish homework when I study online.

Of course, not every student benefits equally—some may become lazy without the structure of school. Still, for many students the advantages of attending classes from home make it a valuable option.

Is it a good idea to choose a career at a young age? I believe it is an excellent choice. In many places, students are expected to have an idea of their future career by the time they start high school. Schools often offer specific courses designed to guide them toward a particular path. This early direction helps students focus and make practical decisions about their education and future work.

First, deciding early lets students explore which careers interest them before they finish high school. Knowing some possible options makes it easier to pick the right subjects and set clear goals. Second, it helps students decide which diploma to aim for. For example, some systems offer an advanced diploma that requires nine SOL exam passes and a full set of classes, while a standard diploma requires six SOL passes and the required classes. When students enter high school, their counselor can explain the differences and recommend which diploma fits their career plans.

Third, high school programs give students the basic classes they need in grades nine and ten. These foundation courses are designed to build skills and knowledge so students can move more quickly into specialized subjects in later years. By taking these early classes, students gain experience and a clearer idea of their strengths and interests, so they are better prepared for the last two years of high school.

If a student keeps the same career choice or decides to change their mind, teachers and counselors are available to help. They can advise the student about the benefits of different careers, including the expected income and job opportunities. This guidance helps students choose a realistic path that matches their goals and gives them the best chance to succeed after graduation.

During grades eleven and twelve, students usually face more challenging courses required for graduation. These upper-level classes are meant to prepare students for the diploma they chose and for life after high school. Counselors play an important role in arranging the right mix of classes so students meet the requirements for either the advanced or the standard diploma and stay on track for their chosen career.

In conclusion, starting to think about a career at a young age is a valuable approach. High school can prepare students for what they want to do after graduation, whether that means going to college or attending a vocational school. Early planning gives students knowledge about possible careers and helps them turn their dreams into real plans. Because teachers and counselors support this process, I think students should begin considering careers when they enter high school so they can work toward a better future for themselves and their families.

Some school districts offer programs that let high school students finish in three years instead of the usual four. This can be a good option, but it is especially difficult for students who have recently arrived from other countries. Newcomers often face language barriers and cultural differences, so understanding lessons and keeping up with classes can be very hard. If you do not speak English well, it takes extra effort to pass courses and meet graduation requirements in a shorter time.

I came to this country with little English, so completing high school in three years was a real challenge for me. I worked hard because I wanted to build a better future for my mother and little brother. Passing the SOL Algebra 1 exam was one of my proudest moments. That success showed me that even with problems and family responsibilities, it is possible to graduate early if you are determined.

Some people believe curfews are an unnecessary interference in young people's lives. They think rules that restrict when teens can be outside are an intrusion. Authorities say curfews are meant to keep young people safe, but many teenagers and parents do not like being told what to do or when to be home.

Curfews usually stop teens from being out after 10 p.m. on weekdays and after midnight on weekends. In practice, officers may stop or question teenagers found on the street after those times, which some see as unfair. The intention is protection, but the result can feel like control.

I believe homework clubs at school are very helpful because they give students time and support to understand their assignments. In a club, students can work through problems more slowly and ask questions until the ideas make sense. They can also finish tasks before going home, so they do not have to worry about homework later. When teachers who enjoy teaching run these clubs, they can offer extra explanations and encouragement to help students improve their grades.

Some pupils fall behind or do not understand certain lessons. Homework clubs allow these students to catch up and sometimes even complete the unit they are studying. Those who make good progress can assist classmates who are struggling or who cannot attend the club, creating a supportive learning environment.

Homework clubs can also be a good fit for teachers who like giving extra help. Some teachers prefer to spend more time helping students solve problems and correct mistakes, and they are willing to stay after school for that reason. While a few teachers only focus on teaching during class and then leave, other teachers enjoy working with students outside of regular lessons and find satisfaction in seeing them succeed.

There are practical reasons why homework clubs matter for families too. Children who have busy schedules with sports or other activities, or who have responsibilities at home such as caring for younger siblings because a parent works or is ill, may not be able to complete homework at home. If after-school buses are available, these students can attend the club and finish their work. Also, when there is extra time at the end of a session, teachers can use those minutes to introduce new topics, giving students a head start on future lessons. Overall, after-school homework clubs are a positive addition to schools.

Dear Manager,

I am writing to ask for the chance to visit your company and learn about the computer-related work that interests me. Exploring a role in computing is a challenge I am excited to take on. This opportunity would help me follow my dream and build a better future for my baby boy. I know it may sound personal, but I am determined to prove what I can do and I believe I deserve the chance to show it.

Computers and technology are used in almost every factory and business today, so having staff who understand them is essential. I have studied computer skills for six years and earned a degree. After that I returned to college to study web design and completed a master’s course. I also took part in a typing competition and won, which shows I can work quickly and accurately. I can create websites and I am familiar with several programs used in web development.

Beyond technical skills, I bring energy, a positive attitude, and strong customer service experience. Before I became interested in computers, I worked for many years in a salon cutting hair. That job taught me how to communicate with people, stay calm in difficult situations, and build good relationships with customers. I believe these strengths would make me a good salesperson or a helpful team member in your company.

Working at the same place for twelve years taught me responsibility and commitment. I love seeing people happy with my work and I take pride in doing things well. Even if I do not know something at first, I will learn it. I am patient and persistent because I know learning new skills takes time, and the reward at the end is worth it.

When I was young, a manager once said I was too inexperienced and suggested I be let go. That hurt, but it also motivated me to prove myself. Today I am more capable and confident, and I hope you will not make the same mistake by overlooking me. If you give me this opportunity to visit and learn, I will show you how hard I work and how much I want to grow.

Technology continues to change industries, and I want to be part of that change. If you choose me for this program, I will not only learn but also share knowledge with others. Thank you for considering my request. I look forward to the possibility of learning from your team.

I disagree with the idea that a positive attitude can fix every problem. There are many situations in life where optimism alone is not enough to change difficult realities.

For example, when someone moves to a new country and is on their own, staying positive is hard. If you do not speak the language well and have no support network, daily life becomes a struggle. If you are undocumented, you do not receive the same benefits as people born here. You might have to hide from the police and it can be nearly impossible to find a good job because of your legal status.

Another situation is the loss of a close family member. If you are in a different country and cannot travel to see them, grief can be overwhelming. In such cases it is unrealistic to expect someone to feel positive while they are mourning and unable to be with their loved ones.

Discrimination is also a powerful reason why optimism may fail. People from other countries can face unfair treatment because of their skin color or because others assume they only came to make money and will leave again. Many immigrants risk their lives to build a new life, but some locals do not understand that and treat them badly. It is very difficult to stay positive when you are constantly judged and mistreated.

Of course, there are reasons to be hopeful: family, friends, a steady job, or finishing school can bring happiness. But sometimes people face financial hardship and cannot rely on friends for help because they have no resources, or they discover friends are dishonest. That makes it hard to keep a positive mindset.

In short, trying to be positive is valuable, but it does not solve all problems. Real hardships—such as being an immigrant separated from family, facing discrimination, or losing a loved one—can make it impossible to remain optimistic all the time.

Working hard to move past what you have mastered helps you acquire new facts and skills. For instance, you can learn how to explore different parts of the world, discover how cars are manufactured, or study how factories operate. These kinds of lessons add practical knowledge that you did not have before.

Making the effort to learn more also leads to deeper and more advanced knowledge. For example, you might learn how to teach science more effectively, study space and astronomy, or even experiment with transforming a car into a robot. These challenges push your abilities and open doors to new fields.

Finally, trying to go beyond your current skills develops an open mind. You can learn how to write a clear essay, gain the ability to coach a team, or understand what it takes to be a person in public office. Such experiences help you think more broadly and accept different viewpoints.

In conclusion, making the effort to learn beyond what you already know is beneficial because it brings more knowledge and a more open mind.

I believe cell phones should be switched off during lessons. When important things happen at school we can still let our parents know, but if phones stay on in class students will be distracted and not pay attention to the teacher. When pupils are looking at their screens instead of listening, learning suffers and sometimes accidents or dangerous situations can happen in the classroom.

Phones are useful for emergencies, though: if something serious occurs at school we should be able to call our parents right away. I disagree with the idea that most people only repeat what they already know and refuse to grow. Staying in the same habits all the time stops personal development, and there are several reasons why trying new things is important.

First, experimenting with different paths can improve your future. If you always do what is familiar, you miss chances to learn new skills or find a better career. For example, my sister used to spend her time on unproductive activities and seemed to have no direction. After a serious talk with our mother about planning her future, she changed her habits and studied hard. Now she is a doctor. Her life improved because she stopped repeating old routines and decided to try something new.

Second, don’t be afraid to do things differently. Fear of change can keep people from starting important projects. My father was once too afraid to start his own business because he believed it would be very difficult. I encouraged him to take the risk and try a different approach. He worked hard, and now our company is doing well. His willingness to change made a big positive difference for our family.

Third, always acting the same way or "being yourself" without challenge can limit what you learn about the world and yourself. My mother often said you should be yourself no matter what, but I think this advice can be misleading if it stops you from improving. If you never push yourself or try new things, you will not discover your full potential or understand different parts of life.

In conclusion, I do not agree that most people only repeat what they already know and refuse to grow. We need to think about our future, be willing to change, and try new experiences rather than staying comfortable with the same old habits.

Everyone has freedom, and if we want something for our future we must work for it. By studying hard and putting in effort, we can reach the goals we set. Families play an important role by encouraging children to study and plan for their future. When parents support their children, it is easier for them to make good decisions and develop. If family support is missing, it becomes harder to choose and grow, so we must then support ourselves.

At the same time, people should listen to advice from their family because they usually want what is best and can guide us based on experience. But final decisions must still come from the individual. To build a good future, a job, or recognition, having someone who supports you helps a lot; if not, you need to become your own supporter.

People should be open to others’ ideas but keep control over their life. With patience, persistence, and courage, anyone can reach their goals. In short, everyone should make their own decisions while accepting wise advice and working hard to create a better life.

Being true to yourself in a world that keeps changing requires a strong mindset. Many people will disagree with your choices, and others will overanalyze everything you say or do. If you want to rise above your current place, you will need to make difficult choices and keep moving toward the achievements you want. Time keeps moving, and the more effort you put in, the more you will gain — a point many people fail to understand. Success does not come without work. Think about LeBron James: his place at the top is the result of steady steps, clear goals, support from family, and constant effort. The opportunities are there; you have to reach for them.

Some say being yourself in a world that constantly tries to shape you is the highest achievement. I do not think the world alone changes you — you change your life through your actions. You will face distractions and make mistakes, but those errors help you learn and move closer to your aims. If you take the easy route, you will get easy results that may not last. But when you work hard from the beginning, later progress becomes easier and you will be grateful you started.

That short conversation made me think differently, and by the end of the term I had improved my grade to a B. I did not know I could do it, but by doing what was needed I succeeded. Others can only show the way; you must be the one to take the steps.

You can do so much if you ask before it happens to you or your family, because if it happens you know how to confront the problem for yourself or with the people you care for and love. There are some options you can do to confront the type of problem you experience.

You can't help others if you don't stay in silence and ask if you can't help or do something for the person who is experiencing some problems, and what type of problem it is, because some problems could always be deadly.

Some people don't have families. You know why? Because they don't let people help with the problems they have. That's when people try to solve for themselves, but in some cases you need help. You can't live without help; it is something that you have to understand. You sometimes need help because if you are in real trouble you will be dead.

It is important to learn from other people's experiences because you might face the same situation someday. Knowing how someone else handled a problem can make you better prepared and less afraid. If you hear about someone who went through something similar, it is sensible to ask what happened and how they solved it. That advice can help you act quickly and avoid panic if the same situation occurs to you or someone close to you.

A good source of practical experience is older family members. For example, when your grandmother shares a problem she faced and the steps she took to solve it, you gain useful options for the future. Hearing her reasons and what worked or failed shows you what to try and what to avoid. This knowledge is valuable because it gives you choices and helps you make better decisions when a similar issue appears.

It is better to ask and learn before a problem happens. If you seek advice in advance, you will know how to respond and what resources are available, so you can act for yourself and protect the people you care about. Without prior knowledge, you may not be able to handle certain situations or take the right steps to solve them.

You also cannot help others effectively if you stay silent. If someone is experiencing a problem, ask questions to understand the situation and whether you can assist. Some problems cannot be solved alone and need clear communication to find a solution.

Finally, some people refuse help and try to manage everything by themselves. This can leave them in real danger. It is important to accept help when necessary because in serious trouble, refusing assistance can lead to worse consequences.
