When people need advice, they often ask more than one person. They do this because making a good decision can be hard, especially when they are stressed, upset, or very happy. In such situations people may feel confused or panic and find it difficult to think clearly. Asking many people seems helpful, but it can also create more confusion because each person will give a different opinion. If you receive too many different suggestions, you might not know which one suits you best.

I think it is fine to ask others for their views, but we must also use our own judgment. When someone gives advice, consider what they are saying and whether it will be good for you. Ask yourself: will following this cause problems? Does this fit my situation? If you still need help, choose someone who is close and trustworthy, like a reliable friend or an adult you respect. Their opinion can guide you, but you should still think for yourself before deciding.

A simple way to find a good solution is to ask just two or three people and then reflect on their answers. If none of those suggestions seem right, trust your own thinking and pick the best option. Always try to find a helpful, honest adult who really wants to support you. If that person agrees with your choice, you can feel more confident about following it.

For example, I once had to plan a birthday party and choose dresses for everyone, but I had very little time. I felt worried and asked friends, cousins, family members, and teachers for ideas. I got so many different opinions that I became more confused. Finally I talked with my older cousin. She explained a clear plan, helped me organize my time, and we managed to finish the preparations in a week. The party went well. From that experience I learned that asking too many people can waste time, and it is better to consult someone you trust or rely on your own judgment.

In summary, the best ways to make good choices are: think carefully by yourself, ask a trustworthy adult for advice, and believe in yourself and in God if that is important to you. Parents and trusted adults often want what is best for you, so their guidance can prevent problems later. Use other people’s opinions as help, but make the final decision with your mind and heart.

Many schools run after-school programs where older students help younger ones with schoolwork and other activities. These programs are useful for children who struggle with certain subjects or need extra support. Older students can teach topics they have learned already or explain areas they once found difficult, which also helps them review and deepen their own understanding.

Younger students benefit because they receive more attention and challenge than they might get at home or in a busy classroom. With guidance from older peers, they can finish homework during the program, so their assignments are not late and they return home with their work done. This lets them relax, play, or spend time with family without worrying about unfinished tasks. Over time, completing homework regularly can help them stay organized and improve their chances of doing well in school and later finding good jobs.

The arrangement also creates a cooperative environment. If a younger student finishes early, they can assist others, and older students can focus on more complex questions or projects. Peer tutoring often makes lessons easier to understand because the language and examples used by students are closer to the learners’ experiences. Working together lets both age groups complete tasks more quickly and enjoy the process more.

A good program balances study and free time. Children should not be stuck doing homework all afternoon; mixing learning with play keeps them motivated and gives them energy. Some students will go outside to play while others continue studying, which keeps the program lively and prevents boredom.

Because of these benefits, more schools should offer structured after-school help led by older students. Such programs support learners of all ages, strengthen academic skills through teaching and review, and create a friendly environment where students help each other succeed.

Many people accept Winston Churchill’s idea that "success consists of going from failure to failure without loss of enthusiasm." They believe experiencing setbacks teaches important lessons, helps people prepare better, and deepens their understanding. Although some disagree with this view, the basic point remains: failure can push someone to try again and improve.

Some people worry about failing and think it shows weakness. However, fearing failure does not stop others from learning. In fact, many who have faced mistakes use those moments to learn new skills and to work harder. They focus on improving themselves so they will not repeat the same errors. This determination shows that failure can motivate positive change rather than prevent it.

Others say failure is only a temporary event and should not be celebrated. When someone fails a test or does poorly at a task, they often keep trying until they succeed. From those experiences they take valuable lessons and rarely lose their drive. This willingness to continue, despite setbacks, fits well with Churchill’s idea about maintaining enthusiasm while moving toward success.

It is also true that failing does not automatically lead to success. To turn setbacks into progress, a person must pay attention to what went wrong, learn from it, and make a real effort to improve. People who do this usually see better results the next time they try. Through practice and persistence, their performance improves.

In conclusion, failure is a natural part of life and an important teacher. If we accept our mistakes, study them, and keep our determination, failures can help us reach our goals. Rather than being ashamed of setbacks, we should use them to build strength and maintain enthusiasm for the future.

Influence affects many parts of our lives. Some people choose their friends or behave in certain ways because they want money, popularity, or connections with rich and powerful people. They believe those relationships will solve their problems, give them a good life, or help them find jobs. But this kind of influence can be dangerous if it leads you to rely on others or follow them without thinking.

Peer pressure can make someone do things they would not do alone. Friends might encourage you to steal, lie, or even harm someone because they are seen as "the most popular" at school or in the neighborhood. If you accept these actions without asking yourself why, you may end up in trouble. Many people have gone to jail after following bad advice from friends. That is why you should be careful and not make important choices quickly or just to fit in.

Influence can be used for good or bad. It can help you earn money, build healthy friendships, and do helpful things for others. True friends do not push you into illegal or harmful behavior. If someone tells you to do something that could get you into trouble with the police, at school, or at home, they are not a real friend. Real friends support you and stand by you when you need help, not when they want you to hurt others or break the law.

If you want to influence others in a positive way, act with kindness and responsibility. People follow those who show good behavior more than those who are popular for the wrong reasons. Being proud of bad actions does not make you a good role model; it only brings problems like jail, broken relationships, and loss of trust. Make decisions that reflect your values and think about the consequences before you act.

If you want others to trust and believe in you, you must change your influence if it is harmful. The right kind of influence can help you reach your goals, like finding a job or improving your social life. Employers and other organizations often look for people who show responsibility and good behavior. If your influence is negative, it will harm your future opportunities.

Always choose to be a positive influence. Help friends and family, and do things that benefit others. Avoid following people who encourage bad decisions. In the end, good influence protects you from trouble and opens doors toward a better future.

Ralph Waldo Emerson once wrote that keeping your true self in a world that often pushes you to become someone else is one of the greatest achievements. I agree with his view because staying true to yourself requires effort, planning, and courage, and it leads to real personal success.

First, knowing who you are and what you want helps you make better choices about your future. Before you face problems at work or with institutions in your country, you should have a clear idea of your goals and organize your life to reach them. This preparation makes it easier to handle difficulties and to find the right path in education, careers, or personal projects.

Hard work is essential to becoming the person you want to be. When you put effort into your goals, people around you notice it — friends, coworkers, and family will respect you and feel proud. Working hard also builds your character and gives you the confidence to make important decisions. To support your individuality, you must choose carefully, act responsibly, and treat others with respect. These habits help others be happy for you and encourage strong relationships.

Working on your own abilities is especially helpful for personal achievement. Individual effort develops the qualities that make you unique: your personality, skills, and values. In some teams, not everyone gives their best and some people only do the minimum to get by. If you rely on others who do not work hard, your progress may slow. That is why personal commitment and continuous effort are so important. If you stop working, you will not reach your goals, but if you keep going, your future will improve.

A true accomplishment comes from steady dedication over time. If you remain focused and work every day, you will see the results and become someone who matters in the world. Success does not come quickly, but persistence brings noticeable rewards.

In conclusion, being yourself in a world that tries to change you means preparing for your future, working hard, and making wise choices. Never lose hope if you face setbacks; keep working and stay positive. By doing this, you will organize your life, become the person you want to be, and achieve the accomplishment Emerson describes.

I disagree with Emerson’s idea that once a person feels defeated they cannot grow. From my experience, setbacks do not have to stop someone from improving. Instead, how a person responds to failure matters more than the failure itself.

First, many people let a setback make them give up, and that prevents any progress. For example, imagine a manager whose sales start to fall. If they only focus on the decline and believe there is no way to change it, they may stop trying new strategies or products. That attitude makes them feel discouraged and less able to move forward in their career. Instead of quitting mentally, looking for alternatives could lead to recovery and growth.

Second, being criticized or getting poor results often causes people to lose confidence and avoid trying again. A friend’s harsh words can make someone doubt their choices and decide not to improve. The same happens in school: a teenager who fails a test might feel so bad that they refuse to study for a retake. This kind of thinking limits opportunities to learn. Accepting feedback and trying again creates the chance to do better next time.

Third, fear of repeating a bad result stops many people from doing what they love. They worry the outcome will be the same, so they avoid another attempt. But repeating an activity with the lessons learned from the first try usually leads to better performance. Experience helps you notice and fix previous mistakes, so persistence is important. You must believe in yourself and keep going despite setbacks.

In conclusion, you should not give up just because you feel defeated. No matter how many times you fail or how hard things get, there are always new chances to start over. Trust in your ability to try again, and you will continue to grow.

I agree with Emerson’s idea that "to be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment." Remaining true to yourself matters for three main reasons: it leads to real achievements, it allows honest living, and it lets you take charge of your own life.

First, originality and independence bring progress. Society needs people who follow their own path — philanthropists who work to reduce poverty, inventors who create technologies like the car, the internet, and computers, and innovators who improve health and safety. When individuals refuse to simply copy others, they can produce important breakthroughs that benefit everyone.

Second, being yourself means living honestly and meaningfully. When you act in ways that reflect who you truly are, you build trust with others and avoid pretending to be someone you are not. This authenticity brings deeper relationships and a stronger sense of purpose than trying to fit the role the world expects of you.

Third, owning your life gives you control over your decisions and future. Making your own choices about work, values, and health leads to a more satisfying and balanced life. Personal responsibility makes achievements more rewarding and life more fulfilling.

Some people claim it’s easier or safer to follow instructions from others, but creating your own success, staying authentic, and directing your life are essential for human development. Life is like a story that each person writes; choosing to be yourself means writing your own meaningful chapter.

I believe that schools offering distance learning are an excellent option for many people for several reasons.

Some people want to complete their studies but cannot because of practical difficulties. They often do not have enough time since they must work, pay bills, and handle other responsibilities. Others leave school to support their families, spend more time with relatives, look after younger brothers or sisters, or take jobs to bring income into the household.

Studying from home is a better choice for students who want to continue their education after high school or enter university. It lets them combine work and study, so they can earn money to pay for their studies and still move toward their future goals. Many degree programs are expensive and some parents cannot afford them. With distance courses, students can work to cover costs while keeping up with their classes.

Also, learning at home can help some students focus more and feel less stressed. Being in a familiar environment—having a snack, worrying less about travel, and organizing study time—can make studying more comfortable. Distance learning gives people free time to do other tasks and manage their daily lives.

In summary, remote classes are a better option for many because they allow people to work, care for children or family, and have personal time, all while finishing their high school or university studies. Distance education makes it possible for those who otherwise could not complete their education to reach their goals.

Achievement makes students more hard-working than praising students. For example, let's say you try to work very hard; if the teacher praises another student, the first student may give up or become upset. Students need achievement to get more work done.

Praising is not a bad thing, so this is another reason why people should pick achievement.

People should rely on real achievement to build self-esteem. Achieving goals pushes people to work harder, learn new skills, and strive for results. Some people argue that praise helps confidence and learning, but praise alone can make students complacent and less willing to put in effort.

First, achievement motivates greater effort than empty compliments. For example, if a teacher praises a student too quickly, that student may stop trying or become discouraged when challenges appear. Students need concrete accomplishments to keep working and improving.

Praising someone is not always harmful, so it is understandable why some favor it. Still, choosing achievement is better overall. Imagine asking a class to complete an art project. If one student finishes a strong piece and others only offer praise, that may not inspire everyone. But when classmates are encouraged to succeed, the accomplishment becomes part of the school’s memories and encourages ongoing effort.

Finally, reaching goals usually brings more lasting happiness than simple praise. Achievements often lead to higher marks or visible progress, which strengthens self-worth more than being told you did well without real results. In short, self-esteem is more often built through genuine achievement than through praise alone. These are the key reasons to prefer achievement for developing self-esteem.

Some people say that a positive attitude is the secret to success. I both agree and disagree with this idea. On one hand, optimism can help people overcome obstacles and reach their goals.

For example, Michael Jordan faced a big setback when he did not make his high school varsity team. Instead of giving up, he stayed determined and worked harder. That mindset helped him develop into one of the greatest basketball players. Another example is the rapper DaBaby. Early in his career many doubted him, but he remained humble, kept believing in himself, and continued to improve. Today he has several gold and platinum records and a large fan base. His positive outlook and persistence played a part in his success.

On the other hand, being positive is not always the best approach. In dangerous situations like war, optimism alone can be risky because soldiers must be alert, realistic, and prepared for threats. In those conditions, a cautious and practical attitude is more important than trying to stay upbeat.

In conclusion, a positive attitude can sometimes open the door to success, but it is not a universal solution. Different circumstances call for different mindsets, and sometimes realism and preparedness are more useful than optimism.

Winston Churchill’s famous line about success being a journey from failure to failure without losing enthusiasm is one I agree with. Experiencing failure is an important part of learning. People sometimes think they must rush through everything, but moving too quickly often causes mistakes. Setting clear goals helps you improve each time you try.

Respecting and listening to others is also crucial. When you fail, advice and support from other people can guide you and make your next attempt better. Failure teaches new skills and shows you what needs to change in your life. It is not a final defeat but a chance to grow.

I also believe trying to do many things at once usually does not work. If you focus on one task and take your time, you are more likely to succeed. The key idea in Churchill’s quote is persistence: do not give up after one or two failures. By trying again and again, you improve because everyone makes mistakes while learning. You cannot know how good you might be at something until you keep practicing and refuse to lose enthusiasm.

Ralph Waldo Emerson’s idea about being yourself can be difficult for anyone, but it is especially hard for teenagers. When you are young, you begin to see the path your life might take, and that makes the choice to stay true to yourself more important — and more stressful.

A caring family makes this choice easier. If your parents watch over you, support your choices, and guide you, you are fortunate because many young people do not have that help. Teenagers who grow up without family support often face more problems than those who have a stable home. They must decide whether to become responsible, make their family proud, and prove they can succeed without much help — or to follow a dangerous path that could lead to prison.

When there is no support, many young people try to find money any way they can so they can eat and help their relatives. To “be yourself” in this situation means to take responsibility, think of your family’s future, and give your younger brothers and sisters chances you didn’t have. Choosing this route while still young is very difficult because you have to leave the past behind and work hard to avoid returning to the same place.

Those who make that decision early learn how to be independent and how a mature person behaves. Life is tough, and only those with strong minds usually endure. To be yourself, you must be mentally strong.

They can learn from the small mistakes that they make. They can grow up from society. In China there are so many reasons that make you grow up.

In China, Emerson’s idea about growth is not always accepted. Ralph Waldo Emerson wrote that “Unless you try to do something beyond what you have already mastered, you will never grow.” While this may be true for some people, I disagree with the idea that trying new challenges is the only way to become more mature. People are different and grow in many ways. I will explain three reasons I disagree: learning new things can make you develop, small details or mistakes can teach important lessons, and everyday life events in society can lead to real growth.

Trying new things can certainly help a person grow, but it is not the only path. For example, my mother came to America without knowing English. She studied the language for three years and now she can speak a little. Her life changed because she learned something she had not known before, and that improvement made her more confident and independent. Her story shows that learning new skills or knowledge can lead to personal development, but it also shows that growth does not always come from some dramatic leap beyond what you already master; steady learning also matters.

Small things can also cause people to grow. In science, a tiny mistake in an experiment can ruin the whole result. Students who make such an error often face criticism from teachers and must think carefully about what went wrong. Dealing with that small failure teaches them attention to detail, patience, and responsibility. These lessons are important and can change a person’s attitude and abilities. So even small events or errors, not only big accomplishments, can be the reason someone becomes more mature.

Finally, many changes come from life itself—work, marriage, and having children can force people to grow. School life is different from the real world: at work, you learn that hard work is not the only way to succeed and that you must collaborate and adapt. Getting married and becoming a parent bring new duties and responsibilities. When you must care for a family, you understand what responsibility really means. These everyday experiences in society shape a person and help them become an adult.

Emerson’s sentence fits some people, but it does not describe everyone. People can grow by learning new things, by learning from small mistakes, and by living through social responsibilities. In China there are many ways to become more mature, and trying to do something beyond what you already know is only one of them.

We achieve more when we keep working toward our goals instead of doing nothing. If we take action and try many things, we are more likely to reach the aims we set for ourselves. A good example is Thomas Jefferson: he accomplished a great deal in his life, including writing the Declaration of Independence. He did not waste his time relaxing while others waited for him to act.

When we decide to change our lives, we usually set goals for each year. Then we keep trying to meet those goals step by step. This continuous effort becomes a habit; we stay active and do not stop. On the other hand, many people waste time and never finish what they start. Everyone has something inside that motivates them to move forward, and this drive is important to reach success.

Around us we can see new phones, shoes, and televisions every year. Behind these improvements there are people who worked hard and kept making small changes. Society moves forward because individuals keep doing things, improving generation after generation. We often act with a purpose, even if we do not notice it every day. When people appear idle, others may think they are wasting time, but steady effort shows progress.

Education is a clear example of how doing things leads to accomplishment. Going to school, then college, and later finding a career requires continuous work. Each step is an action that helps us gain knowledge and improve our life. Family and friends often push us to keep going, especially when we feel like giving up. Their encouragement helps us take the next step.

A common situation is summer break: if someone stays home playing video games, eating, and avoiding chores, parents usually complain. They will tell you to stop playing and start helping with the dishes or find a job. That push can be the turning point to begin accomplishing goals instead of wasting time.

So yes, we accomplish more when we are always doing something. Even small actions matter, and by keeping active every day we move closer to our goals.

People should make their own decisions rather than always following experts or authorities. Being independent allows you to gain personal experience, set your own rules, and avoid constant interference from others. Although some people prefer to rely on those with more experience, I believe starting on your own is better because it helps you grow, become responsible, and ultimately succeed.

First, making your own choices helps you learn from your mistakes. When you decide for yourself and something goes wrong, that error becomes a lesson. These lessons build real experience and teach responsibility in a way that advice from others cannot fully provide. People who see that you have learned from your own failures often respect you and believe you will achieve more in the future. By facing challenges alone, you strengthen your character and increase your knowledge in practical ways.

Second, creating and following your own rules gives you control over your life. If you set the rules, you know what to expect and can plan accordingly. When you follow someone else’s rules, you may not fully understand their reasons, and that can lead to confusion or regret. Personal rules reflect your values and goals, so they guide your decisions in a consistent way. Choosing your path helps you become more confident and smarter about handling your responsibilities.

Third, being independent means fewer people will interfere in your plans. When you are on your own, you are the person in charge of your decisions and actions. Others with more experience might try to correct or control you, directing you down routes you do not want to take. This interference can be frustrating and can stop you from following your own direction. By working alone, you can focus on developing skills in your job, studies, or business, and gradually become an expert who leads others rather than being led.

In conclusion, people should make their own decisions instead of always following experienced others. Starting from zero and learning through trial and error builds strength and skill. Making your own rules helps you stay organized and sure about what you do, while being independent prevents others from constantly controlling your choices. For these reasons, it is better to stand alone at first, learn from your experiences, and become the person who guides others in the future.

I believe working in groups is the most effective approach for students. You might wonder why this is true. For one thing, many learners benefit from hearing other people's ideas. I enjoy listening to classmates’ opinions because their suggestions often shape how the assignment should be carried out. When students have opportunities to share their thoughts, they gain confidence and feel less afraid to speak up.

Still, some students prefer to work alone so they are not interrupted by questions. Those who choose solo work often already know their topic and have a clear plan. Working alone allows them to proceed at their own speed, which can help them finish on time without relying on others.

Group work, however, makes it easy to split tasks into manageable parts. For instance, one person can handle a certain section, another can design the presentation, and someone else can gather research. Breaking the project into pieces lets each student pick the part they find easier or feel more skilled at, which improves the overall quality of the work.

Working in groups also helps students meet new people. Sometimes teachers assign groups randomly, so you may end up with classmates you have never met before. Collaborating with new peers exposes you to different ways of working and organizing ideas. For example, a new teammate might create a T-chart to list pros and cons, which helps decide which side of an argument to focus on. Learning these methods can change how you approach tasks in the future.

Another advantage is that group projects can be completed more quickly. When roles are clear, everyone concentrates on their own portion and the work progresses faster. If someone finishes early, they can offer help to a teammate who is falling behind. A student working alone might need more time to finish everything, but in a group, others can volunteer to assist with difficult parts.

In conclusion, group work teaches students to listen to different viewpoints and encourages cooperation, which makes it a very effective way to study. Some people will still argue that working by oneself is better because it fosters independent decision-making and helps students learn how to produce work without assistance. Despite that, I believe the benefits of collaboration make group work the best choice for most situations.

Working in a group has more advantages for me than working alone. When people cooperate, they can share information, support one another, and reduce stress. If I work by myself, I must rely entirely on my own ideas, and I can become confused or frustrated without anyone to help. For these reasons, I prefer group work.

First, group work makes it easier to finish tasks on time because everyone contributes. When people divide the work and talk about the problems together, the job moves more quickly and we learn from each other. Sharing knowledge helps the whole team understand the task and meet deadlines.

Second, being in a group gives me more help from others. If one person does not know an answer, someone else can explain it. This kind of support improves everyone’s learning because we can discuss different solutions and correct mistakes together. That encouragement also increases my motivation to keep working.

Third, working with other people is less stressful. When a problem is difficult, I do not have to solve it alone; teammates can offer ideas and advice, which makes the situation calmer. It is comforting to know that help is available when I am unsure how to proceed.

On the other hand, working alone has clear drawbacks. I must defend and develop my ideas by myself, which can be hard. If I get stuck, there is no one to explain or suggest alternatives, so confusion becomes more likely. Finally, doing everything on my own can be frustrating, especially if my solutions are not good or I fall behind.

For these reasons, I think group work is more helpful than working alone. Sharing tasks and supporting each other makes learning easier and less stressful.

My friend Generic_Name was supposed to do her work but she always got distracted by her TV show. If she had decided to turn off her TV she would not have been distracted by anything and she could have been successful in her online class.

Students who attend classes from their home do not have anyone reminding them to complete the work. Some of them forget to get it done and end up with incomplete work. This year I am taking an online class and sometimes I forget that I have to do all my requested assignments. By the end of last week I got a bad score because I didn't complete my Vocabulary assignment. If I had put an alarm every day to remind me that I have to study and complete my assignments I could get a better score.

Some others will say that attending classes from home can be a good idea because they can work on it at any time. However, others may say that it is a bad idea because they can get bad grades. Some classmates that are taking online classes aren't reading all the directions that the class is giving; they are just doing the work without reading, and that can affect their grades. Having bad grades can make you not pass your school year, but if we make an effort we can be great.

For some students it is a consideration to take online classes, but at some point it can affect their education. There are many students who have online classes and are falling behind because they don't have enough help, and some of them because they are not doing the work. If schools provide after-school help for online classes, it will be helpful for all students who need to be more successful and feel more comfortable while they are doing their work, and it would also let teachers check if students are able to pass.

Many students who live far from their schools choose to take classes from home. However, I believe learning entirely online is a bad idea because it can distract students, lead to unfinished work, and cause poor grades.

Online learning makes it easy to become distracted. I know a friend named Generic_Name who needed to pass an online math course to graduate. One evening around 6:00 pm I went to her house and found her computer open with the class on, but she was watching a TV show instead of doing the assignments. She enjoyed the show so much that she kept putting off her schoolwork. If Generic_Name had turned the TV off and focused, she would have finished her tasks and probably done better in the class.

Studying at home also means there is no one to remind you about deadlines, so some assignments get left incomplete. I am taking an online class this year and I sometimes forget to do the required tasks. Last week I received a low score because I did not complete a vocabulary assignment. If I had set a daily alarm to remind me to study and finish my work, I could have improved that grade.

Some people argue that home-based classes are good because you can work at any time. Others reply that this flexibility can cause low marks. For instance, several classmates in online courses do not read all the instructions; they rush through tasks and then get poor results. Having bad grades may make it hard to pass the school year, but with effort students can still improve.

Taking online classes may seem convenient for some students, yet it can damage their education if they lack support or self-discipline. Many students are falling behind because they do not receive enough help or they do not complete their work. If schools offered after-school support for online learners and teachers checked progress more often, students would feel more comfortable and would be more likely to succeed.

Once, a close friend of mine was addicted to many drugs — cocaine, marijuana, cigarettes, alcohol and others. One day he asked me which school I attended. When I said Generic_School, he asked if he could come with me. I agreed. He told me he was exhausted from that life and wanted to become someone different. From that moment he began to change. Now he studies to become a doctor because he wants to help others find a better path. This story is why I agree with Emerson’s idea about individuality: it proves that actions, not words or other people’s opinions, shape who we become.

Being true to myself means not letting other people decide my future. If I want to change or pursue a particular job, I must follow what I truly believe, not what others say. For example, if I decide to be a teacher and people tell me it is unimportant because of low pay — that teachers only earn $1,000 a month — I will not let that stop me. Their discouragement may come from their own failed attempts or fears, but the world is always changing. I need to show them by doing the work and staying committed that their negative view is wrong. That is why it is important to ignore those who try to confuse or discourage me.

There is a clear difference between talking and doing. I can say I will change and make many promises, but unless I act, nothing will happen. If I simply boast about my plans without changing my behavior, I will not help anyone — not even myself. On the other hand, if I quietly work on improving my life and then people notice the difference, they will ask what happened. My actions will speak louder than words and become my greatest achievement.

Even when I believe in myself, I must stay focused. I am human and I can make mistakes or lose my way without concentration. Some people enjoy seeing others fail and will try to distract me with jokes or temptations, like claiming school is boring so I will stop studying. I must resist those influences and prove through my dedication that I aim to be more than someone who only seeks fun.

In conclusion, choosing individuality is not easy, but it is powerful. Believe in yourself, do not pay attention to critics, show the difference between talking and doing, and remain focused on your goals. That is how becoming someone different becomes a real accomplishment — the world needs people who change for the better.

These things improve skills, raise academic results, and make college applications stronger. For example, spending weekends volunteering at a hospital or helping in a library gives practical experience and shows commitment. Yes — my school should start a single after-school homework club because many students need extra help to complete and understand their assignments. If teachers stay after school to work with students on class homework, those students will better grasp what they learned in class and will be less confused when a test comes. With support from teachers, students can study more effectively and are more likely to earn higher scores.

However, not all students take advantage of the help offered. Sometimes a teacher stays late and waits for students who were asked to remain for help, but those students do not show up. This frustrates teachers because they gave up personal time to assist them. When students are repeatedly late or fail to complete work even after being given extra time, some teachers stop offering extensions. They want students to understand that finishing homework on time affects their grades, and they may be less willing to give second chances if the same problems continue. A dedicated after-school homework club would make clear when help is available and could reduce the burden on individual teachers who currently give up their free time without reliable attendance.

Some students finish their homework quickly and could help classmates. If these students volunteer in the after-school club, they can assist others who are struggling. Peer support can be useful, because classmates sometimes explain things in simpler or different ways. But this approach has challenges: when students work together without supervision, they may talk or play instead of helping. Some students also dislike getting help from peers because the explanations differ from the teacher’s method, or because it is harder to explain how they arrived at an answer. Teachers often ask students to show their reasoning, and if a student copied a classmate’s work, they may not be able to explain it. The homework club should include teacher supervision to avoid copying and to make sure explanations are clear.

If teachers and student volunteers staff an after-school homework club, overall achievement could improve. Some students forget to do assignments at home or simply do not understand them. Having time after school to complete homework with guidance will reduce those problems. There are subjects where students rarely bring work home, yet later say they had too much to do and forgot; a homework club provides a set time and place to finish assignments so they do not fall behind. Still, some students prefer to finish work during class time when they have free minutes, and teachers should allow that choice. For those who remain, the club offers an alternative: either work with peers or stay with a teacher if they want more formal help.

Parents can also play a role. When teachers contact parents to ask that a child stay after school for help, many families will encourage attendance. This increases the chance homework gets completed and prevents students from saying later that they had no idea about missing assignments. To motivate participation, the school could give small rewards or recognition to students who consistently attend the club and finish their work on time. Positive feedback helps students feel proud of improving their grades.

Homework clubs in other schools show that regular practice and teacher guidance lead to better test performance. Homework is a main way students learn and prepare for exams, so skipping it makes tests more difficult. Some schools do not have homework clubs and assume every student understands assignments, but that is not always true. Students sometimes claim they left work at home or did not bring it because they had no time; a school-run club would reduce these excuses. Finally, many volunteers try to help peers but do not always receive thanks. A structured after-school program can organize volunteers so their time is used well and the students who need help actually get it.

In short, creating one after-school homework club would give students a reliable place to get help, encourage timely completion of assignments, and support better grades. With teacher supervision, student volunteers, parental support, and a bit of recognition, the club could solve many of the problems that now keep students from doing their homework and succeeding in class.

I support the idea of having half days because they allow teachers to organize enjoyable activities and give students a break. When classes end earlier, pupils have extra time to finish homework or catch up on classwork they did not complete during the day.

Some teachers favor half days because they believe students can go home, rest, and study more effectively. However, others oppose the idea because they worry about leaving students at home sooner. I think a compromise is possible: the school should avoid repeating the same routine every day. Varied schedules and activities would keep students engaged and make half days more effective.

Another point in support of half days is that the school gains additional time to prepare for the next day. Teachers and staff could use those hours to plan lessons, organize materials, and improve the learning environment. This preparation helps the school provide better education, which can make students more productive in life.

In conclusion, many people agree with half days because they offer students time to rest and study while giving teachers opportunities to design fun activities and prepare for future classes. With balanced scheduling and variety, half days can benefit both students and the school.

Imagine if students who are sick could stay home and join classes online. That would be very helpful for those who cannot attend school because of illness or hospitalization. Some people have serious health problems, such as cancer, and being able to study from home lets them keep up without risking their recovery. For these students, remote lessons are a big support.

Still, not everyone uses this option honestly. Some say it is fine to miss school whether they are sick or not, and they skip classes even when they are healthy. Others genuinely need online learning but face problems: some schools charge extra for remote lessons, so unwell students must pay even though they cannot take part in sports or other activities. This can be unfair, and it also worries parents who want their children to learn but cannot afford the fees.

I remember when I was five and had a bad cold. I did not want to go to school and cried, but my grandfather convinced me to go. He told me about his own childhood, when there were no online classes. He worked very hard despite his difficulties and later became a doctor. His story made me change my mind, and I went to school that day.

Now I am eighteen, and I am grateful to my grandfather for pushing me. His example taught me that education often requires real effort and sometimes difficult choices. Online classes are a useful tool for those who truly cannot attend, but staying home should not become an easy way to avoid learning. In the end, it is the commitment to education, supported by family and hard work, that helps people succeed and make their families proud.

I understand how vital it is for public servants to support their communities—by supplying necessary goods, using tax revenue to build schools, and assisting people in need. Has technology had a negative or positive effect on people's lives? I believe its impact has been more harmful because many people cannot control their use of devices. Today, many forget how pleasant life can be without constant technology. We can still enjoy simple activities like playing outdoors with friends, visiting libraries, or spending time in nature. Some argue that children should have limits on computer and phone use, while others say teenagers should not be restricted because technology helps them learn. I agree that teenagers need boundaries, and parents must monitor what their children do online.

Those who oppose limits claim teenagers gain useful skills and knowledge from unrestricted access. However, others point out that young people often cannot finish tasks without relying on digital contact. I think face-to-face conversation is important because it helps you get to know someone and strengthens relationships. Meeting strangers online is risky — not everyone has good intentions. Some parents mistakenly believe their children are only playing harmless games, but online interactions can be more complex. Talking or playing with someone online should be limited until the child knows the person well.

Another problem is buying many things online without knowing the seller, which can be dangerous. Some websites honestly sell what they advertise, but others exist only to take money from buyers. If you plan to buy online, make sure the website is safe. Online shopping has also reduced the time families spend together outside the home. Since big sites like Amazon and eBay appeared, people often buy everything from the internet. Scammers take advantage of this trend by creating fake websites to cheat customers.

To help children spend less time with technology, parents can encourage outdoor activities, meetups with friends, or family outings. Making kids form friendships only through online games or social networks is not healthy. It is necessary to know someone well before chatting or playing with them online, because sometimes people trick children into doing harmful things.

For these reasons, I believe technology should be restricted for children. If parents choose to give a child a phone or computer, they must set clear limits and supervise usage. Technology also makes it harder for people to complete tasks without digital help, and online risks like scams and strangers are real. Overall, parents need to put boundaries on technology to protect their children and preserve a healthier way of life.

Big companies could benefit from this change in different ways—not only financially but also by improving support for employees and the community. Of course, some people will see disadvantages and not everyone will agree, but many companies could gain long-term advantages beyond immediate profit.

Schools could also follow a similar approach, though with adjustments since a school is not a business. For example, school days might be extended by two hours on some days, but this should not be mandatory for every student or teacher. If people understand the reasons and accept the change, this adjusted schedule could help save energy and resources. As a result, the environment would be better protected.

The key point is to find the right way to change hours so that energy is conserved. With careful planning and public support, these schedule changes can help provide needed services and lead to greater success for businesses, schools, and the environment.

If you try again at something you have already attempted and it did not work the first time, do not be discouraged. The more you practice, the stronger and more confident you become. Stay calm, keep your courage, and believe in yourself — opportunities will open up if you do not give up. Trying new things shows you what you are capable of; success depends on your determination. Do what you truly want and do not be guided only by other people's opinions, because no one else controls your life.

I do not agree with Ralph Waldo Emerson's idea that repeating something you have done before is wrong. Failing at an attempt does not mean your life is over or that you cannot grow. If you really want something, you will try again and again, even after many losses, and you will not stop until you reach your goal.

My father is an example of this. He is a singer who is very strong and knows what he wants. Once, he took part in a big music project and on the day of the performance he lost his voice. Still, he did his best and succeeded that day. After the show, many people contacted him with different opportunities, and now he is a well-known artist who has grown a lot. This shows that if you keep trying and you believe in yourself, you can improve and find success.

I can relate to this personally. When I came to the United States I did not speak any English. Everything was difficult: my homework, my projects, even communicating. But I did not give up. I kept working hard, tried many things, and I am still improving. Some people think that being an expert from the start guarantees a good future. Others say that spending too much time on one goal can waste your life. I believe that continuing to try what you love is worth it.

Many people stop after they fail, but others keep trying until they succeed. Always do your best and do not give up. If family or friends say you will not grow, do not believe them; you are stronger than you think. Keep working on what you love and prove to others what you can do. Keep faith in your efforts — I disagree with Emerson on this point. Everything depends on you, so never stop trying.

I believe technology increasingly shapes people’s lives and mostly helps us in everyday tasks. Each year new tools appear that make many activities easier. Technology lets us keep in touch with others, play games, and talk to friends no matter where they are. It is useful for work, too: you can apply for jobs online, use maps to find places, or order items so you do not have to go to the store. Long ago these things were not possible, so it is clear technology brings many advantages.

Because of this, it is important to learn how to use devices and services. If someone does not understand technology, they may struggle to do simple things. For example, many jobs require using a computer, and using a smartphone needs some practice. People often ask friends or family for help, so knowing how to explain and teach others is valuable. We should use technology for positive purposes and avoid using it in harmful ways; think before saying yes to everything and make responsible choices.

At the same time, there are negative effects if technology is not used carefully. Children can become too absorbed in devices, which can affect their daily life and behavior. Even adults must set limits and think about what they are doing. It is also wise to consult people who know more when you are unsure, so you do not make mistakes or put yourself at risk.

Overall, modern technology gives us many possibilities. With a phone or a computer you can do a lot: work, study, play, communicate, and manage banking tasks online. But we must use it responsibly, set boundaries, and be aware of the consequences so technology improves our lives instead of causing problems.

People often wake up feeling happy because something good has happened, or they simply find themselves in a cheerful mood. Sometimes people try not to think about feeling down; they prefer to stay positive and want others to feel the same. Other times, friends plan fun activities to lift someone's spirits rather than focus on what made them upset.

There are also times when people do not pay attention to feelings, or they expect someone to just cheer up. In reality, everyone has bad days. A person might be grumpy after waking up or upset because their parent was angry at them for something they did not do. Many people feel sad often, while others keep a positive attitude most of the time. It is unclear why some people get angry easily, even without a clear reason.

When someone is sad or being bullied, others should try to help and make them feel better. Kindness matters: be friendly to everyone and confide only in people you trust. Do not share private things with people who are fake or unkind. If a difficult situation happens, it can be a good idea to tell a teacher or another trusted adult so you can get support. We should try to comfort those having a hard time instead of ignoring them.

People should aim to be happy and avoid harmful behavior. Be yourself and believe in what you can do; do not give up on your goals. If someone tells you that you cannot succeed, they might not be a true friend, so distance yourself from those negative influences. Don’t let other people’s words make you sad—work hard, choose real friends, and stay positive. At school, try your best and keep a good attitude; if you are unhappy there, others might think it is the teacher’s fault or just that school is boring, but doing your best helps you and those around you.

People should make their own decisions. I believe everyone must choose for themselves because it is their life and their responsibility. When you decide for yourself, you understand better why you are doing something and what the result might be. Making your own choices gives you a greater sense of freedom and control over your life.

Deciding on your own is important for several reasons. First, when you make your own decisions you learn more about your likes, your limits, and your goals. This self-knowledge helps you act in ways that suit you best. Second, choosing for yourself usually makes life simpler. If you follow your own plan, you do not have to live with regrets for someone else’s choices. You are more likely to feel calm and satisfied when your actions match your wishes.

It is often hard to accept other people’s decisions. Their priorities and values may be different from yours, so their choices might not work well for you. If you and another person both follow decisions that you do not agree on, it can cause conflicts and make life more difficult. That is why each person should decide what they want to do rather than rely on someone else to choose for them.

Making your own decisions also means being responsible for what happens. This responsibility can be freeing because you know the reasons behind your actions and you can learn from the outcomes. Even if a choice turns out to be wrong, it becomes a lesson you own, not someone else’s mistake.

In short, people should make their own decisions because it leads to more freedom, clearer understanding of what to do, and a smoother life. It is our life to live, so we should be the ones to choose how to live it. Choosing for yourself is better than living by other people’s choices.

People often ask for advice about practical things, especially how to play a sport better or how to do their homework. For example, a teacher or an older student can show you how to solve assignments and explain the steps so you understand the work.

Many requests for help come from students who are new at school. When someone is unfamiliar with the routines or classes, they ask others for guidance. Classmates and teachers should try to help them by explaining the rules, showing where things are, or giving tips on how to succeed.

Advice can also come from coaches or friends who want you to improve in sports. They can teach techniques, suggest exercises, and encourage practice to help you get better. In the same way, if a student is doing poorly on a test, a teacher might recommend staying after class for extra help or offer ways to prepare for a retake.

Even with bigger goals, people need advice. If you want to buy your dream car, someone experienced can explain what to check, how to drive it safely, and what steps to take before you buy. Clear guidance helps people make better choices in many areas of life.

Yes, I agree with the idea that three simple words can reveal a lot about our feelings.

First, be anxious. A large number of people carry many worries about their jobs, tasks, and problems. Constant pressure builds up in their minds, and past experiences can leave strong impressions that affect how they feel now. Many do not show these emotions openly; they keep them inside because they are ashamed or afraid to share. Because of this, they feel stuck and unable to make changes in their lives.

Second, feeling. Some people hide their feelings and stay isolated with their thoughts. They are unsure about what they want or need, and this confusion makes them afraid to speak up. They worry that if they act wrongly, things will never get better. This fear and uncertainty stop them from moving forward and from expressing what is really happening inside.

Third, not believing in oneself. Sometimes people lack self-confidence or self-respect, so they depend on others to do things for them. They may send someone else to handle tasks because they feel embarrassed to do them themselves. This reliance on others can prevent them from growing and facing their own challenges.

Despite these difficulties, life is not impossible. Everything changes over time: our lives, friendships, responsibilities, and emotions. You should not be ashamed to ask for what you truly need or want. Nobody is perfect, and making mistakes is part of learning. If you choose the right direction and work on improving yourself, you can become better. Accept your errors as lessons, make positive choices, and keep trying without letting fear or shame control you.

It also helps with communication between languages by translating words and sentences, which makes it easier to connect with people from different countries.

We use technology to call or message friends, family, and parents. Some argue that it makes people lazy — that they do not move or do anything physical — but this is not entirely true. There are machines and apps for sports and exercise, and technology helps us find information and work opportunities. Many jobs can be done online, so people can work from home if needed. For students, technology is useful for writing essays and taking quizzes, tests, or exams. Schools now include many kinds of technology to support learning.

Technology was created to make tasks simpler. For example, we can take standardized tests like SOLs online instead of using paper, which can make the process easier and faster. Of course, one downside is that some devices and services are expensive to buy.

Mobile phones are a well-known part of technology because they let us communicate without being at home — a call or a text is enough. Overall, technology is so widespread that it affects almost every part of the environment around us. It benefits both young people and adults. From designing jewelry to building houses, much of what we do today depends on technology.

Disadvantages: in a group there will always be a person that wants to be just playing around and doesn't like to do any type of work, just have fun. You will finish your work faster and the way you want the work to be done, but some disadvantages are you will not have fun because you have no one to be with and it will be difficult to have a lot of ideas. I think working with a group is more beneficial because there will be more people at the presentation helping you and you will feel more secure with your work.

Working with a group with the people you trust you learn that friendship is always good for you; have that confidence that people you like being with help you to increase in your life. Today I want to talk about the differences between working in a group and working alone, and explain why I prefer working with others.

Both group work and solo work have positive and negative points. I like group work because teammates can give you new ideas and different ways to solve a task, and it can be more enjoyable to do the work together. Of course, one downside of group work is that there is often someone who does not take the task seriously and prefers to joke around instead of helping. Still, working with a team usually brings more energy and shared responsibility.

If you work alone, the main advantage is that you can do the work exactly the way you want and you do not need to follow other people’s opinions. You can finish tasks more quickly and with your own style. However, working by yourself can become boring and lonely. You may have fewer ideas because you do not have others to discuss and develop thoughts with. Also, being alone too often can affect your personality; people might think you do not like social interaction, and this could lead to misunderstandings or even social isolation.

I believe group work is more useful, especially when you have to present something. If many people know the project, they can all help during the presentation and this makes you feel more confident about your work. Working in a team also helps you improve communication skills, self-confidence, and social skills. You meet new people and can form friendships, which makes tasks more pleasant and supports your personal growth.

Learning to work with others teaches respect for different ideas and how to cooperate. Think about team sports: you cannot play football or basketball alone, so you need to develop teamwork to be successful. In real life and in many careers, being able to work in a group is important. Trusted teammates can become friends who support you and help you improve in ways you cannot do alone.

For example, imagine you are driving on a highway and run out of gas. If you prefer to be alone, you might have to push the car by yourself and risk getting tired or causing an accident. If you are used to working with a group, you could rely on others for help: some could push the car, someone else could stop traffic a little, another person could call for assistance. A team makes this kind of unexpected problem easier to handle.

Working alone is sometimes fine depending on your personality. Some people enjoy focusing by themselves and can perform well without others. But there will be moments when teamwork is necessary because some tasks cannot be completed by one person only. Being a good team member brings respect and lasting friendships; when you help others, they will want to work with you again, and you will feel useful and valued. These feelings are harder to achieve when you always do everything alone.

In conclusion, while both ways of working have their place, I think working in a group offers more benefits overall. It helps you solve difficult problems, learn social skills, and build confidence and friendships. We should try to be more social and include others so everyone has friends and does not feel alone. Helping and respecting each other will make our future better.

I believe that taking classes online or through video chat is a good option for students. For some pupils who live far from school, remote lessons may be the only realistic way to continue their education. Online lessons also provide a useful way to communicate and learn when meeting in person is difficult.

There are clear advantages. Online classes are usually simple and quick to join, and they are especially helpful during bad weather. When snow or ice makes roads unsafe and schools must close, students can still attend lessons from home. In such cases remote learning prevents interruptions to education caused by transport problems.

If I had the choice, I would study online because I find it easier to manage and I can learn well this way. Remote classes can give me more free time for other activities and even allow me to have a job while studying.

However, online learning is not perfect for everyone. Some students do not have a computer or reliable internet access, so they cannot benefit from this option. While online education is a valuable choice for many, it is not suitable for all pupils.

I also think that public online schools should be free so every student can join without paying. Because remote courses are flexible, students can often start lessons at times that suit them and not miss important material. Overall, I am in favor of online and video lessons as a helpful way to learn.

Thomas Jefferson’s words urge people not to remain passive but to act so they can achieve important goals and find purpose. He wanted the colonies to decide whether to stay under strict British rule or to join the fight for their liberty.

From my view, Jefferson meant that colonists who had fought and bled in the French and Indian War were treated unfairly. Even after risking their lives, they were kept from settling new lands and were controlled by a king who favoured his wealthy friends. The crown taxed the colonies but showed little concern for their needs; it seemed to value money and authority above the welfare of ordinary people. That injustice made many question why they should obey a distant ruler who did not respect them.

Others, like Jones, warned that if the colonies did nothing they would live as slaves. Families would lose their homes and food, and people could be treated harshly just for standing up to the British. For those reasons, fighting for freedom and justice seemed better than accepting oppression. To die while defending liberty was seen as honorable compared to living as someone’s subject without rights.

Jefferson’s writings and the newspapers of the time helped many Americans open their eyes. His arguments encouraged people to believe they did not have to follow the king blindly, because they were capable of self-rule. By choosing their own leaders and acting together, they could create a fairer society. In the end, a single person cannot change everything alone, but united groups of people can accomplish great things.

Winston Churchill, the former British prime minister, once said that success is moving from one failure to another without deciding to give up. I agree with this idea because failure often comes from wrong choices or mistakes, but it does not mean the end. When we learn from our errors and keep trying, we can reach our goals.

For example, I failed one test, but I kept studying and later passed. Many students who do not pass at first have the chance to retake exams and improve. This shows that failure can be only a step on the way to success if we continue to work.

Churchill himself faced difficulties but still achieved great things, which is why people believe his words. To become someone important in the future, a person needs to keep trying and not stop after setbacks. There are many people who fail at first and later succeed in different parts of life.

Also, support from family, teachers, or friends can help when we struggle. With persistence and help from others, failure becomes a learning experience rather than a final defeat.

No one else could fully understand my priorities and fears, so I had to choose what felt right for my future.

In those moments, people with greater experience and knowledge are expected to decide, even if a child might not agree at the time.

Still, I believe everyone should have the freedom to make their own choices, whether they decide independently or seek guidance from more experienced people. What matters is being aware of the possible outcomes, because every decision carries consequences — and ultimately, you are the one responsible for choosing what is right for you.

Ralph Waldo Emerson once said, "To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment." I agree with this idea. Being true to who you are is difficult today because society often pushes us to follow trends or fit certain expectations. Staying authentic is a real achievement.

Many people try to stand out and show their individuality. For example, musicians, painters, or teachers might work to create something original. A teacher could invent a new way to help students learn—something no one else has tried. That originality can make the teacher memorable. It might succeed or fail, and others may criticize or praise them. Still, the attempt to remain unique is what matters, even if the world has its own ideas about how we should behave.

There are also people who try to change you or judge you negatively. Their opinions can be powerful and hurtful. But if you are confident and do not let their judgments control you, you remain yourself. Nobody is perfect, and everyone has the right to be different. We can learn from those who came before us—family members, famous artists, or innovators—without copying them exactly. For instance, the creator of Facebook was unique because he developed something that changed how people connect. This shows how one person's originality can have a wide, positive effect.

Life follows a cycle: we are born, grow up, work, and then die. While growing up, we face choices that shape who we become. Questions like "What do you want to be when you grow up?" push us to decide how we will contribute to the world. Teenagers choosing a college major are deciding how they might help society. People may criticize these choices, but in the end, their opinions do not have to determine your path.

We only live once, so the decisions we make should reflect who we truly are. It is important to be thoughtful and wise, but also brave enough to be yourself despite pressure to conform. That, I believe, is the greatest achievement.

I disagree with Ralph Waldo Emerson’s idea that simply being yourself in a world that tries to change you is the greatest accomplishment. I believe that becoming successful or fulfilled usually requires more than just maintaining individuality.

First, a person cannot reach major achievements alone. Schools, teachers, mentors, and other people provide guidance, knowledge, and encouragement that are necessary for growth. Without support and instruction, it is difficult to develop the skills and understanding needed to succeed.

Second, working with others and studying in groups helps us explore ideas, solve problems, and test our goals. Collaboration brings different perspectives and information that we might miss on our own. If someone only works in isolation, they may not fully understand their field or how to reach their ambitions.

Finally, to become truly accomplished, a person must learn about the world and keep improving. Continuous study and experience are required to be excellent in any area. For these reasons, I disagree with Emerson: success depends as much on learning and cooperation as on staying oneself.

Deciding whether students should choose a career early is complicated. I believe there are both advantages and disadvantages to committing at a young age, and the outcome often depends on the person and their situation.

On the positive side, many young people have a fresh view of the world. Because they are less set in their habits, they often imagine possibilities that older people cannot see. This creativity and openness can help them pick a career path that fits their passions and allows them to pursue goals others might think unrealistic. Starting early can also give them more time to gain experience and build skills, which could lead to better opportunities later.

However, there are clear downsides. Young students do not always understand the practical demands of a career. Life can bring sudden responsibilities or financial pressure that force them to change plans. For example, a student who needs to work to support family members may have to pause or abandon their studies. These real-life challenges can make early commitment risky because the world they imagined may not match reality.

A common real situation shows both sides. Imagine a 17-year-old in 10th grade who must find a job because their single mother cannot cover all expenses. This student might feel they must give up their studies and future plans to help their family immediately. On the other hand, being young can also create optimism: they may believe they can both support their mother and continue their education, or at least return to study later. The final result often depends on how determined they are and what support they can get.

Some simple ideas follow from this. Young students tend to be more imaginative and willing to try new things. They may think that anything is possible and be ready to chase chances that appear. With time and effort, early commitment can open doors. But the opposite is also true: careers can be interrupted by sudden events, especially when financial or family needs are urgent.

In conclusion, choosing a career early can be good or bad. Age alone does not decide success—what matters more is a student’s determination and the reality of their circumstances. Young people are the future, and many prove critics wrong by working hard and creating opportunities for themselves. Older people may doubt them, but youth today often have the energy and drive to overcome barriers and succeed.

People often let their character be formed by what others think of them. It is natural to care about the opinions of people who matter, such as friends, family, or a partner. Because of this, many are afraid of losing these relationships or of disappointing the people close to them.

A quote by John Lubbock helped me see this more clearly: "Your character will be what you yourself choose to make of it." I agree with him. Some may disagree, but I believe there is truth in his words. We should not allow other people’s judgments, or painful events, to decide who we become. Ultimately, we can choose how to think and how to react, and therefore we can shape our own character. I have seen this in the lives of three close friends—Generic_Name, Generic_Name, and Generic_Name—who let outside forces determine who they became, and suffered for it.

Generic_Name was hurt by violence in his childhood. His parents hit him frequently, and he grew up angry. At school he often used aggression and got into trouble, which made his parents punish him even more. The pattern continued into adulthood. When he married, he repeated the same violent behavior with his wife. His anger, formed by his early experiences, escalated until it ended in a tragic conclusion: he killed his wife and then himself.

Another friend, Generic_Name, let romantic disappointments shape him. When he was young, he fell for many girls who treated him only as a game. After being hurt again and again, he stopped trusting women and stopped taking relationships seriously. He became the kind of person who used others’ feelings, and because of that he missed real opportunities for love. Once he did meet someone who loved him, his damaged view of relationships caused him to hurt that person as well.

The third friend, Generic_Name, allowed other people’s opinions to control him. He constantly pretended to be someone he was not so that people he cared about would accept him. In doing so he lost his true self and never felt truly happy.

These stories show why we should not let bad experiences, events, or other people’s views decide our character. We are responsible for who we become, and we should choose that for ourselves.

Schools should think about allowing phones because they give students tools to complete tasks and save time, as long as we stay focused on our work. When teachers allow phone use for research or class activities, some students take advantage and use them for studying. The same happens in math when I need to check symbols or use a calculator. Allowing phones helps me learn more and work in a way that suits my needs. It also supports teachers by giving students quick access to information.

In the end, it depends on each student. Phones in class can be either a distraction or a useful learning tool. If the school permits them, students should be thankful and use their phones responsibly for schoolwork, not for entertainment, so their grades do not suffer.

I believe imposing a curfew is a good idea because it can keep students safer and prevent loneliness. If young people are off the streets at night, they are less likely to get hurt or become involved in serious trouble. Fewer teens would break the law, and incidents like street fights, robberies, or shootings could decrease. A curfew would at least offer temporary protection for young people.

At the same time, the government should support homeless teenagers. Leaving school early is a serious problem: many dropouts stop trying in class and do not finish their education. Without qualifications, they will find it hard to succeed later and society will not value them. Young people who end up living on the streets face very difficult lives.

With a curfew in place, some teens might be more likely to look for basic jobs or take small steps toward responsibility, which is better than doing nothing. The real issue is attitude—ignoring studies, being lazy, skipping classes, and disrespectful behavior lead to bad outcomes. If teenagers do not change their mindset, they could follow the wrong path. I hope, however, that with help and rules like a curfew, many will improve and succeed in the future.
