I do not support changing the school rule to prevent students from joining sports or clubs unless they have at least a B average. Expecting every student to earn a B in all classes is unrealistic. Many students love participating in extracurricular activities, and making the requirement so strict would unfairly stop them from taking part. A B average can be difficult for some students to reach even if they work hard.

I would agree, however, with a rule that only prevents students with grades of C or lower from participating. A C is easier to attain than a B, and it still shows that a student is passing. It would be more reasonable to require students to have at least a C to be eligible for sports and other activities. This way, those who are doing okay academically are not punished, while students who are failing can be encouraged to focus on improving their grades.

Many students have mostly Cs and still manage their schoolwork well. In my view, students with C, B, or A grades should be allowed to play sports and join activities. Students who have D or F grades, however, should not be allowed to participate until they bring their marks up. Those lower grades mean a student is in danger of failing the year, and keeping them out of extracurriculars can motivate them to catch up.

To sum up, requiring a B average is too harsh. A better approach is to let students with passing grades (C and above) participate, while restricting those with Ds and Fs until they improve. This balances supporting students’ academic progress with allowing them to enjoy activities they care about.

In my science class, we often do experiments that show chemical changes, like when a flame changes color. I enjoy these lessons because my teachers love science and show their excitement. They help us identify things in nature, not only plants but also objects and processes. Many students go to school because they want to become scientists; for some, this was their dream from a young age. To reach that goal they follow methods and discipline, studying specific topics in an organized way.

People who become scientists work hard on their education. They do not simply decide to be scientists overnight; it takes years of study. To be a scientist you must attend school and sometimes college, and you must pass tests. Science requires study and a careful method. There are many kinds of science. For example, science fiction tells stories that imagine new discoveries, major environmental changes, or space travel. These stories are based on ideas about science and exploration. In experiments, scientists use tools and special equipment to examine things—for example, testing the shape of a blade or studying how materials react. When scientists study animals, like cows, they use specific instruments and often several people work together. Without scientists we would know much less about the solar system and the sky.

We also use scientific notation in math. This is a way of writing numbers as a decimal between 1 and 10 multiplied by a power of ten. Scientific notation helps us work with very large or very small numbers, such as powers of ten. For students who want to become professionals like nurses, education is long and structured: they go to college and complete several years of training. I do not know exactly how many years it takes to become every kind of scientist, but education and practice are always needed.

A scientist is someone with expert knowledge in one or more areas. To become an expert you must study and gain experience; you must be bright and active. Some scientific ideas, such as a chain reaction, involve one event causing the next. For example, in a nuclear chain reaction, the splitting of an atom releases neutrons that then split other atoms, creating a continuing process. Scientists were among the first to learn about atoms and how they can split.

I admire science and the people who work in it. Teachers who love their jobs often inspire students to become scientists or work in other scientific fields. If you want to be a scientist, my advice is simple: follow the rules and keep studying. My mother and sister often say not to show off at home and to behave humbly. My sister once asked my advice about her boyfriend; he wanted to study science and she did not know what to do. I told her to follow her heart. If the boy was determined to go to college and pursue science, she should support his dream. When he chose to continue his studies and they broke up, I felt happy that he followed his goal. I think people deserve praise when they follow their dreams.

My general advice for anyone who wants to work in science is to follow your dream no matter what. Study with passion and do not let others stop you. My brother told me that in life no one can do your homework for you—you have to do it yourself. If you want to be a scientist, you must work harder than usual and keep practicing.

Science runs deep in some people; it feels like it is in their blood. If you truly want to be a scientist, do not let anything stop you. Whether your dream is to study animals, walk dogs, or work with other living things, follow it. Life will ask you to change and adapt, but education and hard work will help.

I have also seen how problems among friends can be similar to problems in science: they need discussion and solutions. A friend of mine had a lot of arguments with someone, and she wanted advice. Her sister told her to be careful about friendships. They talked to their mother and discussed the problems and possible solutions. Talking helps, just like scientists discuss experiments and results.

When my sister thought her boyfriend might be cheating, she asked me for advice. I told her not to become too suspicious without proof and to talk openly about her worries. Communication is important; if you keep your feelings inside, you may become confused and unhappy. I am still learning how to handle my own problems, and talking calmly helps me.

In summary, science is important in the world, and those who love it should follow their dreams. Support each other, study hard, and communicate when problems arise. If you want to be a scientist, do not let anyone discourage you—keep learning and work toward your goal.

High school students should not enroll in programs that let them graduate in three years instead of the usual four. These accelerated tracks usually require extra classes after school or during the summer, and often leave no room for elective courses. As a result, students have less time for homework, for being with family or friends, or for enjoying the summer break. They may also miss out on important electives such as foreign languages, nutrition, music, computer skills, or HPE.

In some cases students end up taking two grade-level courses in the same subject during one year, for example English 9 and English 10 together. It is true that finishing high school early can let some students begin college sooner or start working earlier if they do not plan to attend college. However, the fast pace of the three-year programs increases the chance that students will struggle, fall behind, or give up, because they face more pressure and less recovery time. Traditional four-year high school programs do not usually create that same urgency.

For these reasons, most students are better off completing the regular four-year high school program rather than rushing to graduate early.

I think technology is a positive force because it lets people do many everyday things without leaving home. You can buy items online, read books on the internet, and play games with others, meeting new people while staying in one place.

For some people, visiting others is difficult because they cannot drive or travel easily. Technology helps them stay connected by phone calls, video chats, or messaging, so they can say hello to family across the world or keep in touch with friends. People can also find new friends to talk with and enjoy multiplayer games together.

Technology is useful for learning as well. Many people use the internet to study new subjects or to see what others are sharing on social media. Students can use devices and websites for schoolwork and homework help. Schools can guide safe and helpful uses of technology so that teenagers learn how to use it responsibly.

Older adults benefit, too. They can read books online about topics they like, such as history, sports, or hobbies. Learning basic technology skills makes it easier for them to call relatives or join online communities when they want company or information.

Shopping and food services have also improved because of technology. People can order groceries or meals online and have them delivered to their home. This convenience can change daily life by saving time and effort.

Many people use online services for practical tasks like preparing taxes, getting advice, or hiring someone to do them. Technology is especially helpful for those who are shy or anxious about leaving the house; it lets them connect with others who share their interests without face-to-face contact.

There are also entertainment and earning opportunities on the internet. Gamers can play online or download games to enjoy at home. Some people even make money through gaming or other online activities. Teenagers often like to play for long periods, improve their skills, and sometimes earn rewards or income.

Overall, technology can be used in many ways to make life easier and better. It helps people find friends, finish schoolwork faster, handle daily tasks, and work from home when needed. Both young and old can gain from learning how to use technology. For these reasons, I believe technology is a good thing and will continue to be helpful as it develops.

The writer who said "you will never grow" made a strong point about how people behave in real life. I agree with this idea. Many people are not satisfied with what they have, and that attitude prevents personal growth. The main problems are greed, a feeling of superiority, and a desire to have everything at once.

First, greed can harm those who want to progress at work, in school, or at home. For example, my brother dropped out of school because he wanted money quickly. He thought leaving school to work more hours would be the best choice. Later he realized this decision was wrong and now says it was a mistake. His example shows how greed can stop someone from developing skills and opportunities for the future.

Second, some people believe they are better than others, which creates distance and coldness in society. This attitude can lead to rejection and even bullying. I strongly disagree with thinking that only certain people can achieve great things. Humility matters: if one person can accomplish something important, others can too through effort and respect.

Third, wanting everything at once makes real growth impossible. True development is not measured by how many material things you own. Life is often fleeting; to grow, you should learn to appreciate the small things you already have. Education and values help you become a better person with strong principles.

In conclusion, life offers many chances, and you must choose wisely. If you avoid vanity and focus on learning and humility, you can grow and become a good, thoughtful person.

Here are three reasons why most students should not do their school classes online from home.

First, learning at home can be difficult because students lose access to immediate help from teachers. In school, you can ask a teacher questions, get explanations, and receive support right away. At home, when you struggle with an assignment, there is often no one qualified to help. This makes the work harder and more frustrating. For many students, being in the classroom makes learning easier and helps them finish their tasks correctly.

Second, online classes make cheating easier and can lower the quality of learning. When students do work at home, it is simple to copy answers from friends or use the internet in ways that do not show real understanding. This hurts their grades and does not prepare them for exams or future study. Also, students who already passed required tests like the SOL or who keep a high GPA might manage online work well, but most students need the structure and supervision of school to learn properly.

Third, online-only lessons are not right for every age or family situation. Some parents want their children in school where adults can supervise them and where social skills are developed. While online classes could be useful for certain groups—such as college students, very advanced students who have already passed their classes, or motivated learners—making all classes online would not be good for the majority. It may be easier for teachers and for some children, but it would not suit everyone.

In conclusion, schools should not move all student classes to an online-at-home model. Online options can be helpful in certain cases, like college courses or for students who have already proven they can work independently, but most middle and high school students benefit more from in-person instruction where teachers are available and cheating is harder.

Albert Einstein once said, "Imagination is more important than knowledge." I disagree with this idea. I believe knowledge is more important because it gives us the tools to turn imagination into reality.

First, imagination alone is not enough to act wisely. You can dream up many ideas, but without the necessary facts and skills, those ideas may not work. For example, if you imagine writing a story, you need to know about grammar, character development, and how to structure a plot. Knowledge helps you place the right details in the right places, so your story becomes clear and convincing. Without that knowledge, the images in your mind cannot be communicated well.

Second, knowledge helps you plan and make sensible decisions. If you only rely on imagination, you might miss important facts about a situation and make wrong choices. In everyday life, when you go to work you must understand your tasks and use specific knowledge to complete them. Imagination can suggest new approaches, but knowledge tells you which steps to take and which risks to avoid.

Third, in scientific or practical tasks knowledge is essential before you begin experimenting. For instance, if you need to examine a plant in science class, you should first learn about its parts and how to observe them properly. Imagination might help you think of interesting questions, but knowledge gives you the methods and background to investigate those questions correctly.

Another example is a crime scene. Police officers need knowledge to understand the scene, identify suspects, and find evidence. Imagination might help form a hypothesis, but without facts and training, it is impossible to solve the case accurately. Knowledge makes imagination useful and reliable.

Some people argue that imagination comes before knowledge and is therefore more important. Imagination does help us picture possibilities and be creative. However, I think imagination works best when it is supported by knowledge. Knowledge makes our mental images more precise and practical. Different people may value imagination and knowledge in different ways, but in my view, knowledge should come first to make imagination effective.

In conclusion, imagination is valuable, but knowledge is more important because it lets us understand situations, act correctly, and develop creative ideas into real results. Knowledge provides the foundation that makes imagination productive.

Thomas Jefferson’s idea that we should always strive to do more makes a lot of sense to me. Being active and trying new things can spark curiosity in students and lead to better ideas in schools. If we don’t create opportunities for different activities, students may not think in new ways or share useful information with others. Encouraging more projects and events gives people a chance to learn, collaborate, and bring fresh perspectives to their communities.

Adding fun sports or creative activities is another important point. When students take part in enjoyable pastimes, they can reduce stress and relax their minds. Regular involvement in activities helps young people grow and develop skills they will use later in life. At the same time, it is important that they still have time to enjoy being young rather than always being pressured to achieve. A balance between effort and leisure allows students to develop without missing out on the simple pleasures of youth.

Constant work without relaxation can also affect family life. If someone is always busy with responsibilities and projects, they may spend less time with their family and miss important moments. Jefferson’s message can be understood as a call to be active and responsible, but also careful to keep the relationships and memories that matter. We should aim to do more while protecting time for family and rest.

If you have big dreams, working steadily toward them is essential. Doing what you love gives you energy to keep going and improves your performance. The more you practice, the better your results will be. With passion comes responsibility: for example, if you are committed to a sport, you must train consistently to reach a high level. Focus and effort produce progress, and seeing good results motivates you to continue.

I believe Jefferson wanted to inspire people to be creative, enthusiastic, and persistent. He showed that life can be more rewarding when we keep trying, even when we face problems. Being determined and working hard leads to personal growth and happiness. In short, his words encourage us to pursue our goals, take on responsibilities, and never give up. Jefferson’s example reminds us that effort, balance, and resilience are the keys to a fulfilling life.

I believe that self-esteem grows from receiving praise. Compliments help students build confidence in themselves.

Praise from teachers is especially powerful. Almost everyone likes to be praised, and I do not enjoy being criticized by my parents. Like many people, I care about what others say. Young people are sensitive and may react by blaming others or becoming defensive. Instead of scolding, adults should encourage students and highlight their strengths. If a student makes a mistake, it is better to say something like, "I believe you can do this better," rather than simply saying no.

A person’s life is like a short story: the way they think and act is shaped by what they have experienced. Some people face easier times, others cope with greater challenges, and these experiences influence their choices and behavior. When someone has lived through similar events, their story can inspire others and encourage positive change. After going through many situations, people can become a source of motivation for others who face the same problems.

There are many ways a person can be influenced. Not every event or example will inspire everyone. Sometimes an example from another’s life will not resonate, but at other times seeing how someone handled a difficulty can give you confidence when you do not know what to do. A person’s influence can be useful and comforting in moments of doubt.

Examples are only one way to influence others. There are moments when you do not need someone else to push you; you need to reflect on your own situation and decide what is best for you. Personal reflection can lead to choices that improve your life, based on what you believe is right.

We are human and we make mistakes. People must learn from their errors, and there are many ways to encourage someone, but sometimes a person does not even think about looking for an example to follow. Learning by doing and by reflecting on your mistakes is often as powerful as being inspired by someone else.

When people consider inspiration or motivation, they might not notice that they have already faced a similar situation. Because everyone is different, what helped one person may not work for another. Seeing someone else’s experience should be treated as an example to learn from, not a direct solution. You can take the positive parts and adapt them to fit your own needs.

Sometimes it is only a coincidence that two people go through the same circumstance, and instead of feeling inspired they simply feel understood. Recognizing differences in how people handle similar problems can be useful: ask yourself why someone reacted differently and what you might do differently if the situation happens again.

There are times when someone feels touched because their life experience matches another person’s. Identifying with a friend, family member, or even a stranger can be inspiring. Just knowing you are not the only one who faced a problem can have a strong emotional effect and help you move forward.

Having someone to inspire you with their experience can be very helpful. People often think they are alone in their struggles, and hearing a story of someone who managed to overcome the same difficulty can make them believe they can do it too. For some, the idea of having a role model in their head is enough to build confidence.

There will always be good and bad moments in life, and sometimes your actions become the reason others feel inspired. Behavior can influence people, but because of different personalities and ways of thinking, watching someone else do something good or bad will not always change you. Still, being an example is valuable: it can touch others, help them identify with you, and possibly encourage them to act differently and better.

I disagree with the idea that technology isolates us. It gives us easy access to information about books, online stores, games and many other things. Of course, not everything we find online is correct, and some advice will be wrong because nobody can know everything. Still, having access to information is useful even if we must be careful with what we trust.

No one has complete knowledge. For example, I know how to buy books online, while my sister is better at ordering groceries or clothes. She can show me how to shop, and I can teach her how to find and buy books. By sharing what we know, both of us learn new skills. This kind of exchange is one of the main benefits of staying connected.

Technology helps us stay in touch in many ways, not just for shopping or playing games. Social networks and messaging apps like Facebook, Twitter and WhatsApp let people meet, talk and help each other. If access to these tools were reduced, some people would find life less interesting. Many enjoy chatting with friends for hours, and limits on that would feel boring to them. Still, it is healthy to balance time online and offline.

Being connected also keeps us informed about important events in our country, such as fires or earthquakes. Timely information can save lives and help people organize support after disasters. We should be connected with both good and bad people in the sense that we can learn from many sources. Sometimes a person with a bad reputation can still share useful facts, while honest people can teach good habits. It is better to know a few people well than to try to do everything alone.

At the same time, privacy matters. Living entirely online or trusting everyone can be dangerous. Some people give false information that could lead you into legal trouble or other problems. So we should be careful about whom we trust and what we follow. Private time is important, but total isolation is not the answer. Ask questions, connect with others to gain knowledge, and reject advice that seems harmful. Nobody is perfect, and by communicating wisely we can improve our lives without losing our safety.

The Prime Minister Winston Churchill once said, "Success consists of going from failure to failure without loss of enthusiasm." I disagree with this idea. While Churchill’s words aim to encourage people, I believe that simply moving from one failure to another without changing anything is not always good advice.

First, when someone fails many times and keeps repeating the same actions, it is natural to feel discouraged. Continuing to do the same thing over and over without results can be harmful if there is no sign of improvement. Each person must decide whether to keep trying the same approach or to change direction. That decision belongs to the individual and should be based on reflection, not only on blind enthusiasm.

Second, failures play an important role in life and can teach us valuable lessons. But if a person never tries again or never learns from mistakes, they will likely stay stuck and miss future opportunities. Persistence is useful only when it comes with learning and adjustment. Being enthusiastic is important, but enthusiasm alone cannot replace careful thought and new strategies.

It is also wrong to let other people’s negative opinions stop you. Nobody else has the right to say that you cannot succeed. If you have a clear goal and real motivation, you should not give up just because someone doubts you. For example, I want to graduate and get a diploma, then continue to college. I am positive and motivated. If I fail at first, I will stand up and try again, perhaps in a different way until I reach my goal.

Trying again does not always mean doing exactly the same thing. Sometimes life forces us to change methods, and different situations need different solutions. Many people find answers after several attempts because they adjusted their plans and kept looking for options. Companies facing bankruptcy often search for new solutions rather than simply repeating past actions; this shows that failure can be a step toward finding a better path.

In conclusion, do not lose your energy when you meet failure, but also do not follow the idea of repeating failures without reflection. Keep hope and fight for solutions, change your methods when needed, and learn from mistakes rather than assuming that enthusiasm alone will bring success.

Technology has brought people closer and created new ways for us to communicate across the world. It allows friends and family who live far apart to get in touch almost instantly, saving time and making relationships easier to maintain. Many modern inventions, such as video games, also show how technology can be enjoyable and engaging for people of all ages.

One of the most important benefits of technology is that it removes limits on communication. Online platforms and messaging apps provide fast, reliable ways to stay connected, even when people are physically distant. These tools often cost less than traditional methods of contact, so keeping in touch becomes both quicker and more affordable.

Technology has helped solve the problem of weak social connections that once existed between people. Through research and development, scientists and engineers have created systems that encourage communication and interaction. The main aim of these technologies is to simplify life and to build stronger links between individuals around the globe.

Part of this change is how technology has reduced the need to travel in order to see relatives or friends. Mobile phones and video calls mean we do not always need to be physically present to have a meaningful conversation. Another impressive achievement of technology is the speed at which news and information spread; people can learn about events from other countries in moments.

Besides saving time, technology often lowers the cost of communicating. Many services are inexpensive or free, which helps people who want to contact others without worrying about expensive fees. This has made communication more accessible for a larger number of people.

At the same time, some people are skeptical or confused about technology because they have never used advanced devices, or they do not fully understand how to use them. For those who lack basic skills like reading, writing and listening, new technologies can be difficult to learn and use effectively.

In the end, technology can greatly improve communication and daily life, but its benefits are best realized when people have the education needed to use it. Teaching basic literacy and digital skills will help more people take advantage of technological tools, creating a stronger, better-connected world.

Do we achieve more by keeping busy all the time, or does doing less also have value? In my view, students ought to stay active throughout the school year and beyond. Being involved helps us develop abilities, and repeated practice turns beginners into experts. Some people, however, think that taking things easy has advantages, such as avoiding exhaustion and having more time to rest.

People who support constant activity argue that those who regularly practice improve faster. For example, students who play sports build endurance and learn to push themselves. Similarly, when we stay engaged in class tasks and school projects, we grow more skilled and efficient. This experience is useful later when looking for a job: employers prefer reliable workers, and an active record at school or in community service can provide good references.

On the other hand, not everyone agrees. Some believe that staying inactive is better because doing too much can lead to boredom or burnout. Students who do not take part in many extracurricular activities sometimes have extra time to study and to relax their minds, which may improve exam results. For them, avoiding constant activity helps maintain balance and prevents becoming too tired too quickly.

Still, there are clear benefits to practicing regularly. When students follow teachers’ instructions and repeat tasks often, they speed up and make fewer mistakes. This steady improvement can make them more competitive for scholarships and jobs later on. Participation in school life—such as clubs, teams, or volunteer work—also builds a positive reputation, since others can see the effort a student has put in.

Sports specifically add physical and personal advantages. Regular exercise strengthens the body, increases stamina, and encourages discipline—qualities that can carry into the workplace. School sports often give credit or awards, which provide recognition and memorable experiences. They are also a way to meet friends who share active interests, creating social support that motivates continued involvement.

At the same time, rest is important. Getting enough sleep and eating breakfast provide the energy needed to be productive the next day. Students must manage their time so they can be active without becoming exhausted; being active should depend on a person’s energy and choices, not on pressure.

In conclusion, being active generally leads to greater accomplishment and prepares students for the future. It helps reach goals, creates opportunities like scholarships, and can improve career prospects. Yet activity should be voluntary and balanced with rest. When students put effort into participation but also care for their health, they are more likely to succeed now and later in life.

A first impression can be very hard to forget. It can create a strong memory that stays with you for a long time, almost like a mark on your heart. For example, when you were a child and your parents bought you a new toy you really wanted, that moment probably made you very happy and excited. That special feeling is unforgettable. It becomes an important part of who you are and is difficult to change afterward.

The main point of this idea is how important a first impression is for your feelings and behavior. When something happens for the first time and it is meaningful to you, it usually shapes how you see that thing in the future. If an experience makes you feel special or loved, you are likely to remember it clearly. The timing and the intention behind the action also matter. When something happens at the right moment and with good intentions, it can create a strong impression.

I believe first impressions are hard to reverse because they have a strong emotional impact. The first time you feel something strongly, you realize how important that experience is for you. That initial feeling often becomes the standard by which similar experiences are judged later on.

This subject matters because understanding the power of first impressions helps us appreciate why certain memories stay with us. I can speak from my own life: when I was very young, an event happened that made me feel extremely happy and impressed. A city council is considering a curfew: 10 p.m. on weekdays and midnight on weekends for teenagers. If approved, young people who are out later than these times would be breaking the law. I believe a curfew is beneficial because it helps protect teenagers and keeps them from getting into trouble.

Nighttime can be risky. Walking around late, teenagers may not know what dangers they could face, such as being in the wrong place at the wrong time or encountering dangerous people. What looks exciting or “cool” to some teens can quickly turn into a risky situation. If police stop a teenager late at night, officers may question whether parents know where the teen is. If the teen cannot give a satisfactory answer, the police may contact the parents, which could lead to serious consequences.

Parents often worry when their children are not home on time. Teenagers want to spend time with friends, but it’s worth considering whether staying out late is worth causing parents stress or putting oneself at risk. A curfew helps reduce those late-night situations and gives families peace of mind. Darkness reduces visibility, making it easier to be in harm’s way without realizing it, and there are additional hazards at night such as drunk drivers.

A curfew is a law, and breaking it can bring trouble with the police. Officers take these rules seriously because they are meant to protect young people. Parents want their children to be safe and to follow rules, not to lose their trust over a few hours with friends. It’s important to prioritize family responsibilities instead of making risky choices to impress friends.

Respecting parental rules is also important. Curfews encourage teens to think about how their actions affect others and to make safer decisions. When parents find out their child was out late, it often causes anxiety and difficult conversations. Teens can choose whether to stay home or go out, and they should consider the potential consequences of staying out past curfew.

There are plenty of safer ways to socialize, such as meeting during the day, having sleepovers, or calling friends. Rather than sneaking out for food or to be with a boyfriend or girlfriend, teens should stay home or stay in touch by phone. In short, following curfew rules helps teens avoid trouble, keeps parents reassured, and encourages sensible behavior.

The city council has approved a curfew for teenagers.

There should be a curfew for young people because they should not be out on the streets after midnight. On weekends especially, teenagers ought to be home and getting rest. A study shows that adolescents who follow a curfew do better at school, while those without one are more likely to break the law and struggle academically. Why would a young person need to be out late at night? They might be coming back from a party, getting involved in gang activity, or just wandering where trouble happens. At that hour most people are tired and want to be indoors, not roaming around.

If the curfew is put in place, there will be fewer teenagers on the streets at night.

The council in Generic_City has passed a law setting the curfew at 10 p.m.

This means a teen walking alone on the street after 10 p.m. would be violating the law.

If a police officer finds them, the officer can arrest or take them to a safe place. The city made this rule because being outside late at night can be dangerous for young people. Officials expect teens to be at home after the curfew so they are protected.

Some members of the community asked why a rule should control teenagers’ lives. They worry it interferes with young people’s freedom.

Does a curfew keep teens out of trouble?

A curfew helps keep teens away from risky situations, but it needs everyone’s cooperation. Parents, police, and community groups must work together so young people stay safe.

Police can check where teens are and ask about their plans. If an officer finds a teenager alone at night, they can contact the family or take the teen to a safe place. This law is meant to prevent parents from receiving tragic news or emergency calls about their child. For many families, not having to face a sudden loss is reason enough for a curfew.

Teenagers sometimes do not understand the consequences of risky choices. The curfew encourages protection first and helps them get the support they need.

The city council has adopted the curfew at 10 p.m. for these reasons. Teenagers need this rule to stay safe.
